name: E eu, sou o que?
desc: E eu, sou o que? (And What Am I?) is a racial literacy guide created by Ceará's Public Defender's Office Ethnic-Racial Equality Committee. The accessible plain-language booklet equips defenders and public servants to understand and confront structural racism—helping staff correctly identify their racial identity and strengthening respect in interpersonal relations. Launched at units across the state with participation from defenders and technical teams, it functions as an official institutional training instrument shaping administrative practices, public service delivery, and policy formulation toward racial equality and human rights protection.
details: The Ethnic-Racial Equality Committee of the Ceará Public Defender's Office was established in December 2024 as part of an institutional policy focused on racial literacy and anti-racist practices. The Committee’s first concrete action took place in April 2025 with the launch of the booklet "And what am I? A short guide on (your) race." The material aims to equip public defenders and staff members to understand and confront structural racism, drawing on reliable references, accessible language, and an approach sensitive to everyday experiences. The booklet serves as a tool for internal transformation. It encourages teams to engage in self-recognition, correctly identify their race, and strengthen their sense of belonging, thereby fostering more respectful interpersonal relationships. Thus, the booklet establishes itself as a guide for promoting inclusivity and strengthening an institutional culture that is attentive to racial inequalities. The relevance of the material is underscored by the recurring questions that arise in the institution's daily operations. Questions such as "negro or preto?" (terms for Black individuals), "if my mother is Black, am I Black too?", and "is it appropriate to call someone *moreno*?" highlight the importance of providing guidance to teams with clarity, conceptual accuracy, and responsibility. The initiative is directly linked to a public institution, as it originates, is coordinated, and is implemented within the Public Defender's Office of the State of Ceará. The Communications Department, at the initiative of the Ethnic-Racial Equality Committee, is responsible for developing and managing the booklet. Furthermore, the booklet is part of an internal public policy on racial literacy and anti-racist practices, formalized by the institution's leadership.

name: Saúde e direitos humanos das pessoas com deficiência: disseminando conhecimento para fortalecer a cidadania
org: Escola Nacional de Saúde Pública Sergio Arouca da Fundação Oswaldo Cruz
desc: This initiative, led by Fiocruz since 2020, promotes human rights and health literacy for people with disabilities through accessible educational materials developed in partnership with civil society. Available in multiple formats, languages (English, Spanish, French, and accessible Portuguese), and distributed both digitally and in print, the resources use simple language and culturally relevant formats such as cordel literature to reach diverse audiences. By addressing the historical exclusion of people with disabilities, fostering social participation, and combating ableism, the initiative has become a nationally recognized model for inclusive education and communication, influencing public policies, strengthening partnerships across Brazil, and supporting professional training and disability rights advocacy.
details:
"The initiative aims to disseminate educational communication content for literacy on human rights and the health of people with disabilities, as well as to raise awareness of the issue. The material, unprecedented in the country, is created in a participatory manner and brings together knowledge mobilized by the rights of people with disabilities, made available in an accessible way. Its relevance stems from the historical violation of the human rights of people with disabilities, evidenced by various social indicators (unequal access to education, work, health, income, as well as greater vulnerability to violence and food insecurity). In health, although a universal right in Brazil, the needs of this population remain invisible in universal actions and in the production of knowledge.

The target audience includes: people with disabilities and their families; civil society movements; workers and managers in social areas; researchers and professors from postgraduate programs; and public policy makers.

The production consists of various communication pieces, disseminated in simple language and in cordel literature. The booklets and posters were printed for distribution and are also available in digital version in the Arca repository." Fiocruz, in English, Spanish, and French, and with accessibility features in the Portuguese version (subtitles, audio description, and sign language). Its free availability in various formats and languages ​​allows for adaptation to different audiences and territories, enhancing its replicability in other contexts, institutions, and countries.

Developed since 2020, the initiative has been consolidated through continuous interdisciplinary practices and processes, expressing the institutional commitment to knowledge production, professional training, and the promotion of the rights of people with disabilities. Its viability is evidenced by the growing adoption by civil society, facilitated by its availability in a public repository; in addition, municipal, state, and federal actors have been establishing partnerships for printing the booklets and working in their territories.

Because it is developed in partnership with civil society and brings together historically separated social groups, the initiative strengthens social participation, dialogue, active listening, and the sharing of knowledge. It is innovative in several aspects: 1) In its format, by presenting synthetic content, grounded in rights, and in different formats, expanding accessibility and reach; 2) In the process of Production, which promotes collective appropriation, enhances the feedback system, integrates the audiences of the subject matter, and favors dissemination; 3) Dissemination in varied spaces: scientific events, postgraduate programs, basic education schools, libraries, museums, and cultural events, such as Carnival; 4) Commitment to an emancipatory education that values ​​autonomy, protagonism, and social justice. The initiative is developed within a public teaching and research institution, the Sérgio Arouca National School of Public Health, Fiocruz, aligned with its commitment to knowledge production, professional training, and actions of social interest. It also engages with the national normative framework, such as the Brazilian Inclusion Law (Law 13.146/2015), which guarantees the right to communicational accessibility, and the National Policy for Comprehensive Health Care for People with Disabilities, from 2023, which reaffirms the right to participation, information, communicational accessibility, and the importance of the necessary fight against ableism, also highlighted in the "New Living Without Limits" program, which uniquely focuses on the importance of confronting this system of oppression (ableism). Furthermore, it converges with the School's institutional commitment to valuing participation, diversity, social justice, and emancipatory education. And her success led to an invitation from the Ministry of Health, through the Secretariat of Specialized Care, to coordinate the Specialization Course on "Qualifying the Care Network for People with Disabilities." It also led to an invitation from the Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship to coordinate Axis 2 (combating ableism and other forms of violence) of the New Living Without Limits program. The initiative is also aligned with a recently enacted law in the country that established the National Plain Language Policy (Law 15.263/2025).

name: Coleção Olhares Plurais
org: Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) - Programa Justiça Plural
desc: Olhares Plurais (Plural Perspectives) is an analytical bulletin collection by the Plural Justice Programme—a partnership between Brazil's National Council of Justice (CNJ) and UNDP. It democratizes qualified information on human rights and judicial access by translating complex research and institutional experiences into short, high-impact content with innovative visual design inspired by Brazilian culture. In 2025, the collection generated 16 news articles across CNJ and 12 partner courts, reached 38,857 users through 4 social media publications, and generated 31,726 interactions. Featured at four high-level events, it exemplifies how institutional communication can move beyond bureaucratic reporting to become an effective public education and legal literacy tool.
details:
"Plural Perspectives" is a collection of analytical bulletins from the Plural Justice Program, a partnership between the National Council of Justice (CNJ) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). The collection democratizes qualified information on human rights and access to justice.

By translating complex research and institutional experiences into short, impactful content, it broadens public understanding of the challenges and solutions of the justice system. Its guiding principle is to make visible the structuring agendas of the Judiciary, organizing data and diagnoses of public utility in clear language and with an innovative visual identity.

The visual identity, inspired by Brazilian culture, combines institutional standardization and strategic language, making complex themes more accessible and representative. In this way, it facilitates reading, expands social reach, and transforms technical content into more effective instruments of public communication, strengthening institutional didactics.

The collection currently has five editions, published in print and digital versions, available on the Program's official page on the CNJ portal.

- The 1st edition analyzes how the Judiciary institutionalizes - The 1st edition focuses on LGBTQIA+ issues, identifying commissions, policies, and actions to combat discrimination. Its visual identity communicates peace, freedom, and plurality, inspired by the woodcuts of J. Borges.

- The 2nd edition outlines the landscape of human rights structures in the courts and highlights institutional arrangements, gaps, and opportunities for strengthening. Its visual identity reflects sensitivity, uniqueness, and networking.

- The 3rd edition offers an initial diagnosis of the Specialized Centers for Victim Assistance (Ceavs), addressing multidisciplinary teams, services, and challenges of humanized care. Its visual identity incorporates welcoming features and warming colors.

- The 4th edition presents the unprecedented affirmative action of Justiça Plural to recruit professionals from socially vulnerable groups, highlighting diversity, qualification, and institutional innovation in the selection process. Its visual identity reinterprets symbols and reimagines the country, inspired by the work Okê Oxóssi, by Abdias do Nascimento.

- The 5th edition analyzes court initiatives in the context of the Award. Racial Equity, emphasizing progress, commitments, and mechanisms to address racism in the justice system. Its visual identity proposes a green light for racial justice, inspired by the work Efrain Bocabalístico: Oxóssi-Xangô-Ogum, by Abdias do Nascimento.

The Plural Perspectives collection offers a replicable model to strengthen equity in justice systems. The initiative demonstrates how strategic, accessible, and evidence-based content can drive institutional transformations, amplify social change, and bring the Judiciary closer to society, aligning with the United Nations' commitment to "leave no one behind." "The Plural Justice Program is an initiative of the CNJ (National Council of Justice), in partnership with UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) and with the support of the Brazilian Cooperation Agency (ABC/MRE), aimed at promoting human rights, socio-environmental rights, and access to justice for structurally vulnerable populations.

By translating complex research, data, and institutional practices into clear and accessible content, the collection democratizes knowledge and improves evidence-based decision-making.

It also strengthens the articulation between public institutions by offering inputs for the formulation of judicial policies: it transforms institutional initiatives and practices into useful analyses for courts, public bodies, and technical teams.

In addition, it offers diagnoses, guidelines, and thematic summaries that promote the institutionalization of priority agendas and contribute to harmonizing practices and guiding coordinated responses to structural inequalities.

In this way, it acts as a bridge between institutional knowledge, public policies, and society itself, fostering democratic governance and the State's capacity to guarantee rights more effectively, especially to structurally vulnerable populations.

Based on its targeted dissemination strategy..." Targeting high-impact audiences, the collection expands these dialogues to include other strategic actors such as opinion leaders and civil society organizations, promoting transparency, participation, and institutional innovation.

name: Portal de Participação Cidadã
desc: The Portal de Participação Cidadã of Brazil's Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) repositions the institution as the 'Citizens' Court' by placing citizens at the center of public resource oversight decisions. The portal operationalizes citizen participation through public consultations where any Brazilian can vote on social problems and share personal experiences. The first consultation (April–June 2025) attracted 1,341 citizens, 3,360 votes, and 407 narratives, generating five actual audits judged in plenary sessions with participants present. A second consultation gathered 10,359 votes—demonstrating rapid scaling. The initiative combines digital voting, plain language, audiovisual resources, and in-person outreach as a replicable model for meaningful public participation in government accountability.
details:
"The Citizen Participation Portal (cidadao.tcu.gov.br) seeks to position the Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) as the "Citizen's Court," placing the citizen at the center of decisions regarding the oversight of public resources.

Overview and Objectives:
The initiative operationalizes citizen participation through public consultations in which all citizens can vote on social issues and share personal experiences. The main objective is to bring external control closer to society, aligning oversight priorities with real demands, strengthening institutional transparency, and consolidating a model of citizen participation.

Target Audience and Methodology:
Every Brazilian citizen. The inclusive approach combines digital voting, simplified language, audiovisual resources, and in-person mobilizations.

History:
Conceived in January 2025 by President Vital do Rêgo, after a visit to the Court of Accounts of France. First consultation: April 23 to June 30, 2025." 2025. Second consultation: November 19, 2025 to February 1, 2026.

Stakeholders: Civil society, social control advisors, and citizens. At the TCU (Brazilian Federal Court of Accounts), the Secretariats of Institutional Relations (coordinator), External Control, Communication, IT and Digital Evolution, and state secretaries of the TCU.

Proven Results

First consultation: 1,341 citizens, 3,360 votes, 407 qualitative reports. Five themes converted into effective audits (health works, idle properties, INSS [Brazilian Social Security Institute] queues, climate change, highways). Presentation in plenary session with citizen participation.

Second consultation (until January 29): 10,359 votes, 1,259 reports, 2,073 registered participants. 18 problems in 5 themes. Results in plenary session, November 2025. 2026.

Innovation:

Unique integration: digital voting + qualitative reports as equivalent sources.

Concrete actions: voting linked to effective, not symbolic, audits.

Scalability: 206% growth between consultations.

Inclusion: translates technical problems into accessible language.

Replicability: scalable model for Courts of Accounts.

Complete cycle: voting → implementation → public presentation

Participatory democracy: citizen as a legitimate producer of knowledge.

Transformative impact: Transcends communication tool, functioning as an instrument of democratization. Growing numbers suggest that citizens recognize that their voices have an effect. Strengthens institutional legitimacy in a context of crisis of confidence in public structures, seeking to consolidate the TCU (Brazilian Federal Court of Accounts) as a reference in citizen participation in external control. "Institutional Link
The Portal is an activity inherent to the TCU (Brazilian Federal Court of Accounts), the body that oversees federal public resources, transforming citizen participation into a permanent policy integrated into audit planning.

Alignment with Public Policies

OECD Recommendation - Public Integrity: international recommendations to deepen participatory democracy.

Open Government: exemplifies active transparency, invites citizens to participate, and reports results publicly.

Public Modernization: consolidates a state-society model based on genuine listening.

Public Policy Cycle
Citizens vote on issues → TCU conducts audits based on votes and reports → Results in plenary session.

Institutional Collaboration
TCU Units: Secretariats of Institutional Relations, External Control, Communication, IT, State Secretaries and audit teams. State and municipal Courts of Accounts, various public bodies and civil society.

Results
First Consultation:" 1,341 citizens, 3,360 votes, 407 reports. Five themes generated five audits judged in Plenary Session.

Second Consultation (until 01/29/2026): 10,359 votes, 1,259 reports, 2,073 citizens registered to follow the results.

Transformation in Governance
The portal changes how the TCU (Brazilian Federal Court of Accounts) defines its agenda. The technical definition now incorporates citizen participation, reflecting popular demands. Citizens choose themes that affect Brazilians and the resources allocated to issues of high social relevance.

name: Tiny Rathaus / Tiny Town Hall
desc: The Tiny Town Hall is a mobile participation space developed in 2022 by KielRegion GmbH under Germany's Smart Cities federal programme, designed to bring democratic engagement directly to citizens in northern Germany. The mobile unit travels to urban neighborhoods and rural communities, enabling local governments to discuss mobility, climate action, and local development in accessible, face-to-face settings. Since 2022, it has visited 55 locations, hosted approximately 260 events, and been used by the City of Kiel, district administrations, associations, and community organizations—establishing a replicable model for mobile democratic participation that overcomes geographic and institutional barriers to public engagement.
details:
"The “Tiny Town Hall” as a mobile Participation space

The Tiny Town Hall is a mobile participation space designed to bring citizen engagement directly to the people of the KielRegion in northern Germany (including the city of Kiel and the districts Rendsburg-Eckernförde and Plön). Developed in 2022 as part of the federal program Model Projects Smart Cities (funded by the German Federal Ministry for Housing, Urban Development and Building), the initiative aims to strengthen democratic participation and foster dialogue between local administrations and civil society in an open, accessible, and innovative way.

The Tiny Town Hall seeks to make participation more inclusive, visible, and flexible by creating a mobile platform for dialogue, co-creation, and information exchange. It enables municipalities to meet citizens where they are, whether in urban neighborhoods or rural communities, and to address local issues collaboratively. The initiative promotes transparency, trust, and creativity in public communication, offering formats such as mayor’s office hours, workshops, consultations, and cultural events.

The primary audience includes residents of the KielRegion (urban and rural), local associations, schools, and community organizations. It also serves municipal administrations and decision-makers who want to engage citizens in planning and development processes. Special attention is given to groups that are often underrepresented in traditional participation formats, such as youth and elderly citizens.

The project was co-created through a collaborative process involving the KielRegion GmbH, the City of Kiel, and the Anscharcampus Creative Center, supported by additional local actors. The concept was tested in 2021 and officially launched in 2022. Since then, the Tiny Town Hall has toured the region annually, hosting over 260 events at more than 50 locations. Key stakeholders include municipal administrations, civic organizations, and regional networks. Funding comes from the Smart Cities program.

The Tiny Town Hall redefines what a “town hall” can be. Instead of expecting citizens to come to administrative buildings, it brings governance and participation into public spaces, e.g. markets, village squares, festivals – using a compact, transportable structure (approx. 8.6 m²) mounted on a trailer. Its mobility allows for rapid deployment and adaptation to diverse contexts, from dense urban quarters to remote rural areas. The initiative combines physical presence with digital tools (e.g., interactive platforms, QR-based surveys, and touch tables) to enhance accessibility and engagement. By creating a welcoming, creative environment for dialogue, the Tiny Town Hall lowers barriers to participation and demonstrates how public communication can be human-centered, flexible, and playful.
""KielRegion GmbH is a publicly funded regional development company supported by the City of Kiel and the districts of Plön and Rendsburg-Eckernförde, making it a public institution with a clear mandate to foster regional cooperation and innovation. Within this framework, KielRegion GmbH developed the Tiny Rathaus as part of the Model Projects Smart Cities program, funded by the German Federal Ministry for Housing, Urban Development and Building.
The Tiny Rathaus is actively used by the City of Kiel and the districts of Plön and Rendsburg-Eckernförde to engage with citizens on a wide range of topics. It serves as a mobile platform for dialogue, enabling municipalities to inform residents, involve them in decision-making processes, and gather feedback on local projects and policies. By bringing participation directly to public spaces, the initiative strengthens democratic engagement and ensures that governance is accessible and inclusive."

name: EXTRA FAVELAS
desc: Extra Favelas is a journalistic and community-engagement initiative by Rio newspaper EXTRA, developed in partnership with Rio de Janeiro City Council, to strengthen the visibility, dignity, and political voice of favela residents—historically marginalized from decision-making. In 2025, Extra Favelas organized five community debates inside different favelas, an unprecedented step for a major Brazilian media outlet. These events brought together residents, local leaders, and City Council members, creating direct dialogue spaces. The initiative generated over 10 million impressions across print, online, radio, and social media, establishing a model for how established media can recenter public communication around underrepresented communities.
details:
"Developed in partnership with the Rio City Council, Extra Favelas is a journalistic and community-engagement initiative created by the Rio newspaper EXTRA to strengthen the visibility, dignity and political voice of residents of Rio de Janeiro’s favelas—historically marginalized communities that are often excluded from decision-making processes.

Launched in 2024 with a landmark debate at Editora Globo’s headquarters, the project was conceived as both a media brand and a sustained editorial commitment to covering issues affecting low-income communities. In 2025, Extra Favelas expanded significantly, moving from newsroom-centered debates to direct engagement inside the favelas themselves. The newspaper organized five community debates within different favelas, an unprecedented effort for a major media outlet in Brazil and a demonstration of Extra’s intention to serve as a catalyst for social dialogue and public accountability.

These on-the-ground events gathered local leaders, residents, public officials and city council members to discuss priority topics such as public services, health, mobility, safety, education, entrepreneurship and representation. The cycle culminated in the Fórum Extra Favelas, held again at Editora Globo’s auditorium, which brought together experts and community voices to deepen the conversations sparked in the territories. The forum reached millions through print, digital and social-media coverage. 

A central component of the initiative was a hybrid survey, conducted both in person during the community debates and online on Extra’s website, enabling favela residents to identify their most urgent needs and describe aspects of their daily lives. The results of this unprecedented consultation were transformed into a special series of reports and formally delivered to the Rio City Council to help inform discussions on public policy. Council members participated actively in the debates, reinforcing the project’s role as a bridge between institutions and citizens.

Extra Favelas redefines the role of a media outlet in public communication by bringing institutional debate directly into marginalized territories, rather than asking residents to travel to institutional spaces. It combines journalism, civic participation and policy influence, creating a two-way communication channel: listening to communities, amplifying their voices through large-scale media coverage, and delivering their demands to decision-makers. At a time when trust in institutions is fragile, the project innovates by positioning a newspaper as a connector that fosters inclusion, transparency and collaborative governance.""The Extra Favelas initiative is structurally connected to the Rio de Janeiro City Council, which partnered with Extra from the very beginning of the project. The first debate in 2024 was co-organized with the City Council, establishing an institutional foundation for dialogue between legislators and favela residents. In 2025, council members actively participated in the five debates held inside the communities, engaging directly with citizens on issues such as public services, mobility, safety, health and education.

A central element of the initiative—the hybrid survey conducted both in person and online—was formally delivered to the City Council as a tool to inform legislative debates and guide future public policies affecting the favelas. By transforming residents’ demands into structured data and widely disseminated journalism, Extra Favelas provides policymakers with evidence-based insights while ensuring that community concerns reach official decision-making arenas.

The project thus operates as a bridge between public institutions and historically excluded populations, facilitating communication, improving transparency and strengthening democratic participation. Its design is aligned with the Atlas’s goals: supporting inclusive governance by connecting citizens’ lived experiences to institutional action and policy reform."

name: Voices of Resilience: An Interactive Dialogue Between the Public and Local Authorities
org: Department of Strategic and Socio-Economic Development of Sumy City Council
desc: Voices of Resilience is a public communication initiative by Sumy City Council, Ukraine, addressing management burnout and trust erosion caused by war and instability in this border community. The initiative combines motivational training, the UPGRADE transformational management game, and analytical tools to rebuild internal resilience in local government teams and restore bilateral dialogue with residents. The UPGRADE game addresses team motivation, resilience building, and adaptive leadership in conditions of uncertainty—equipping managers to communicate with constituents during ongoing crisis. The initiative demonstrates how internal communication and leadership development directly affect the quality of public governance in conflict contexts.
details:
"The Voices of Resilience: Interactive Dialogue between the Public and Local Self-Government initiative aims to introduce a new approach to public communication, addressing a critical issue in the border community of Sumy. Here, war and constant instability have led to a loss of motivation and emotional burnout among management teams, which undermines team cohesion and reduces the effectiveness of recovery processes. This creates a crisis of trust both within teams and in relations with residents.
The main task is not only to restore the internal psychological resilience and adaptability of LSM specialists, but also to transform their internal resources into a powerful mechanism for bilateral dialogue that strengthens public trust and social cohesion. The target audiences include LSM specialists, heads of KP/KU, OGS, and community residents.
The essence of the innovation: The project uses a comprehensive approach that combines motivational training, transformational games, and analytical reflection. This methodology is uniquely adapted to the challenges of the border region, focusing on mobilizing internal resources on the ground.
The result is an Analytical Document. Unlike a regular report, this document summarizes the insights, requests, and management dilemmas developed by experts during the games. It becomes the basis for public consultation. 
This allows the OMS to transparently present the complexity of decisions, and the OGS to participate in the formulation of joint recovery strategies, integrating public experience into strategic recommendations. The next step is to present the results in a form that is accessible and open to the public: conclusions from the games are converted into visual content for use on community web platforms. Complex management dilemmas are presented with the aim of showing the public the logic behind the decisions taken, rather than just the outcome. This creates safe spaces for sharing information resources, dispels rumors, and builds trust, as the community sees that the authorities also work in conditions of uncertainty and do everything openly out of concern for the well-being of citizens.
This integrated approach ensures that the internal development of local self-government becomes an innovative, open tool for creating dialogue and strengthening social cohesion in the community.""The project is directly aimed at strengthening the human resources and psychological resilience of OMS specialists and managers of municipal enterprises in the Sumy community. They are the main target audience for training (transformational games and workshops). The project is being implemented by the Department of Strategic and Socio-Economic Development of the Sumy City Council. The Department performs a number of tasks related to the direct implementation of the project, such as:
providing analysis of the results of the activities carried out (results of transformation games, participants' reflections after the training, which will subsequently ensure thorough preparation for the formation of the Analytical Document)
 planning events (developing a schedule of events, forming the most optimal combinations of activities for the best assimilation of material by participants), selecting participants. The Department also provides premises for sessions, trainings, and transformational games, namely the Office of Recovery and Development. After the event, it is also responsible for disseminating information on web resources for the public and further publishing the Analytical Document for a wider audience in the community."

name: From Portals to Conversations: Reimagining Public Communication Through Messaging
desc: Chat Nation reimagines public communication by enabling governments to engage citizens through conversational interactions on WhatsApp and USSD platforms. Rather than requiring citizens to navigate complex digital portals, Chat Nation converts government language into plain two-way conversations accessible without smartphones or internet data. In partnership with Kenya Revenue Authority, Chat Nation has enabled over 200,000 citizen transactions per day via conversational interfaces, contributing to onboarding approximately 300,000 new taxpayers. The initiative demonstrates how messaging platforms can serve as primary government communication channels, particularly in low-connectivity and informal-sector environments across Africa.
details:
"Chat Nation reimagines public communication by enabling governments to engage citizens through simple, conversational interactions on widely used messaging channels such as WhatsApp and USSD. The initiative transforms complex public policies, administrative procedures and service requirements into simplified, accessible, two-way conversations that people can understand and act on, without needing smartphones, data-intensive portals or digital literacy.
The core objective of Chat Nation is to strengthen inclusion, trust and participation in public service delivery by meeting people where they already are and communicating in ways that reflect their everyday realities. By converting technical government language into plain, conversational guidance, the initiative reduces friction between citizens and institutions while improving compliance, access and responsiveness.
Chat Nation primarily targets populations that are often excluded from traditional digital government systems, including informal sector workers, small businesses, women, youth, rural communities and low-connectivity users. At the same time, it supports public institutions, such as revenue authorities and government digital service teams, by providing a scalable, interoperable interface that complements existing systems rather than replacing them.
The initiative was developed in 2024 in response to persistent gaps observed in public communication and service access, particularly in contexts where digital transformation has relied heavily on portals and forms that unintentionally exclude large segments of society. Since its development, Chat Nation has been deployed in collaboration with public authorities and ecosystem partners to support policy implementation in areas such as registration, compliance and access to public services.
Key stakeholders include public institutions responsible for policy implementation, technology and digital government teams, civil society and innovation partners and end users who interact directly with the platform through messaging channels. The initiative is designed to align with national digital transformation strategies and Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) principles, ensuring interoperability, institutional ownership, data protection and sustainability.
What makes Chat Nation innovative is its shift from broadcast-based public communication to dialogue-driven engagement at scale. Instead of requiring citizens to navigate complex systems, the system listens, responds and guides users step by step in real time. name: ECoVR
desc: ECoVR is an immersive virtual reality environmental education application developed by the University of Amsterdam, funded by the Dutch Research Council. Targeting high school students aged 15–18, the VR experience makes climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental impacts tangible through interactive scenarios where students' food choices visibly alter virtual ecosystems. A randomized longitudinal study with 226 students across nine schools found that VR participants showed significantly higher environmental knowledge scores—sustained gains one week after the intervention—and made more climate-friendly food choices compared to controls. ECoVR demonstrates how immersive technology can be a powerful public communication medium for translating abstract environmental challenges into personally meaningful understanding.
details:
ECoVR is an innovative virtual reality (VR) application designed to engage high school students in environmental education and pro-environmental behavior. Developed between 2023-2025 by ECoLab and the Visualisation Lab at the University of Amsterdam, and funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO), the initiative targets students in upper secondary education (ages 15-18) and aims to increase knowledge about climate change, biodiversity loss, and the environmental impact of food choices, while also stimulating sustainable actions. Through an immersive VR experience, students learn how individual decisions affect the environment.

The experience has three core components: (1) a lecture delivered by a scientist avatar within a lush digital rainforest and other ecosystems, presenting complex environmental concepts in an accessible, engaging manner; (2) an interactive choice game in which students’ food decisions dynamically alter the virtual environment—unsustainable choices degrade the ecosystem, while sustainable choices restore it; and (3) actionable guidance on environmentally friendly behaviors, emphasizing achievable steps such as reducing meat portions or engaging peers in sustainability discussions.

ECoVR was developed by an interdisciplinary team combining expertise in environmental communication and educational design (ECoLab) and immersive technologies (Visualisation Lab). In close collaboration with high schools and teachers, we validated the experience to ensure the content fit students’ everyday world, aligning with their interests, language, and level of understanding. 

The innovative character of the experience lies in the experiential logic it implements. Through the deliberate combination of immersion, interactivity, and behavioral guidance, the experience reduces psychological distance to climate change, makes the causal impact of individual food choices immediately perceptible, and facilitates the translation of experiential insight into concrete, achievable actions. This approach moves beyond traditional classroom teaching, where concepts remain abstract and distant, by enabling students to “experience” the consequences of their choices within a dynamic, multi-sensory environment. 

ECoVR follows the tangibility-proximity-action framework, which functions as a transferable design principle for sustainability communication beyond this specific VR application, where consequences are first rendered tangible (via interactive game feedback), then connected to users’ immediate contexts (immersive VR ecosystems), and finally linked to actionable alternatives (sustainable behaviors). As a concrete instantiation of this framework, ECoVR demonstrates how immersive, classroom-ready technologies can enhance understanding, engagement, and motivation to act. By offering schools a scalable, ready-to-use tool, it exemplifies the next frontier in sustainability education. "ECoVR is directly connected to Dutch public education and environmental policy goals, particularly the integration of sustainability education in secondary schools. The initiative supports the implementation of educational programs aligned with national curricula on climate literacy, responsible consumption, and environmental awareness. By targeting high school students—future citizens whose behaviors and attitudes are still forming—ECoVR contributes to public objectives of fostering informed, responsible, and active participation in sustainability initiatives.

Furthermore, ECoVR aligns with broader policy frameworks, including the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production, and SDG 13: Climate Action), translating abstract policy priorities into actionable experiences for adolescents. The project has engaged schools as institutional partners and collaborated with educators and educational authorities to ensure the VR experience complements existing teaching practices, reinforcing public commitments to youth engagement and environmental education.
"

name: "Not Alone" - Anti-Cyber-Kidnaping Campaign
desc: The 'Not Alone' (Khong Mot Minh) campaign is a Vietnam-wide anti-cybercrime initiative by the Digital Trust Alliance and the Cyber Security Department (A05), distributed via METUB Network's 5,000+ creator network. Responding to a surge in sophisticated online kidnapping and coercive manipulation scams targeting university students, the campaign used youth-friendly digital formats—music, video, influencer content—to reach Generation Z where administrative warnings had failed. The campaign generated over 1.5 billion views, reaching more than 40 million citizens—nearly 40% of Vietnam's population. Hashtags consistently ranked among national trending topics, demonstrating a creator-led, youth-centered model for public safety communication in digital-native populations.
details:
"Summary of the Initiative

1. Urgent Context
In 2024, Viet Nam faced a rapidly escalating yet largely invisible wave of cybercrime, with estimated economic losses reaching VND 18.9 trillion nationwide. By 2025, this threat evolved into more psychologically sophisticated forms, commonly referred to as “online kidnapping” and coercive manipulation, disproportionately targeting university students aged 18–22 living away from home.
In this context, conventional top-down public communication—often framed as administrative warnings—proved increasingly ineffective in reaching Generation Z. Addressing these risks required a fundamentally different model of public engagement, capable of resonating with young people’s lived digital realities and rebuilding trust in public safety messaging.

2. The Initiative and Partnership Model
The “Khong Mot Minh” (Not Alone) campaign was initiated by the Digital Trust Alliance (DTA) and the Cyber Security and High-Tech Crime Prevention Department (A05), Ministry of Public Security, with institutional support from UNODC and UNICEF. METUB Network joined as the Official Social Communication Partner, responsible for translating legal and policy-based messages into culturally relevant formats and mobilizing social resources to amplify outreach.
The initiative aimed to build a multi-layered digital protection framework for approximately 12 million young people by strengthening awareness, resilience, and self-protection skills in the online environment.

3. Innovation Lens: Why This Initiative Is Transformative
The campaign marked a deliberate shift from one-way information dissemination to a participatory communication ecosystem, anchored in three mutually reinforcing pillars:

a. Policy Translation – Clarity in Action: METUB translated complex law enforcement warnings into popular culture formats, embedding digital safety principles into the campaign’s theme song “Clicking”, short scenario-based videos, and TikTok dance challenges, transforming regulatory knowledge into accessible and shareable content.

b. Youth Inclusion and Empowerment: Rather than positioning young people as passive victims, the campaign empowered them as active contributors, with thousands of students creating original content, artwork, and personal stories, strengthening ownership, dignity, and trust.

c. Proactive Digital Prevention: Through edutainment-based learning, the initiative delivered a “digital vaccine,” enabling young people to recognize manipulation and fraud before harm occurs, shifting the focus from reactive enforcement to active prevention.

Beyond its national scope, “Khong Mot Minh” also served as a flagship satellite initiative welcoming the signing of the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime (“Hanoi Convention”), reaffirming Viet Nam’s commitment to global digital governance and child protection.
Connection with Public Institutions and Public Policy

This initiative represents a practical and scalable model of Public–Private Partnership designed to bridge the gap between public institutions and digital citizens.

1. Public Sector Leadership
The Cyber Security and High-Tech Crime Prevention Department (A05), Ministry of Public Security, provided technical leadership, legal authority, and policy alignment, ensuring institutional legitimacy and consistency with national cybersecurity priorities.

2. METUB’s Role as a Trust Catalyst
Beyond execution, METUB functioned as a trust catalyst. Leveraging its network of over 5,000 content creators, METUB translated public policies into relatable, dialogue-driven interactions. This approach helped soften the perceived distance between law enforcement agencies and young citizens, repositioning A05 from a distant regulator to a credible and approachable protector in the digital space.

3. Policy Alignment and Global Relevance
The campaign directly operationalized Viet Nam’s National Cybersecurity Strategy while simultaneously supporting high-level diplomatic objectives associated with the signing of the UN Convention on Cybercrime in October 2025. The screening of the campaign’s summary video at an official United Nations session demonstrated the role of the private sector as an essential partner in addressing global governance challenges.
"

name: Mulheres em Dialogo
desc: Mulheres em Diálogo (Women in Dialogue) by Instituto Update in Brazil bridges progressive and conservative women around the polarizing topic of public security through research and facilitated dialogue. Using qualitative and quantitative methods, the project maps how different audiences perceive urban violence and gender-based violence, identifying convergence points across ideological lines. A central output is the Narrative Guide—systematizing findings into concrete recommendations for civil society actors, communicators, and educators on framing discussions about gender-based violence with reduced resistance. It is a practical tool for navigating polarized communication environments in Brazil.
details:
"The project “Possible Convergences: Women Weaving Dialogues on Political Security” seeks to establish a dialogue process between progressive and conservative women around the theme of public security, one of the most mobilizing and polarizing issues in contemporary Brazil.

Our approach is hybrid, addressing both urban violence (assaults, organized crime, police, weaponry) and gender based violence (domestic, sexual, femicide, harassment). The objective is to map how these different audiences perceive and elaborate on the issue of security, identifying points of convergence and building repertoires of dialogue that strengthen more democratic and inclusive policies.

Using qualitative and quantitative methods, the project will also seek to understand how public opinion is shaped by competing narratives, especially on social media and among young people, who today consume and reproduce political views through memes, videos, and simplified discourses. In the end, the results will be disseminated in reports, digital campaigns, opinion articles, and a national meeting with organizations and parliamentarians.""Mulheres em Diálogo links to public institutions and policy processes through its engagement with elected officials, legislative spaces, and public debate on gender, democracy, and violence prevention in Brasilia, the nation’s capital. The initiative was designed in response to documented gaps in public policy discourse on GBV, political violence against women, and public security, particularly under conditions of political polarization.

The program engages members of parliament and public officials, primarily women legislators from diverse ideological and territorial contexts—including federal, state, and municipal levels—have publicly endorsed, participated in, or used the initiative’s research and narrative outputs to inform debates on women’s rights, political participation, and responses to violence. This engagement strengthens the connection between women’s lived experiences, research evidence, and legislative agendas.

We also contribute to public policy by informing narrative and communication strategies used by CSO's that interface directly with public systems addressing violence against women, including protection services, justice mechanisms, and prevention policies. The Narrative Guide translates research findings into policy-relevant framing tools that support public institutions and partners as well."

name: BHASHINI: Powering Multilingual AI for Inclusive Public Communication in a Linguistically Diverse Democracy
desc: BHASHINI is India's national AI language infrastructure initiative launched in 2022 by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, positioning language as core digital infrastructure enabling citizens to access public information and services in their own languages. Delivering 18+ AI-powered services including machine translation, speech recognition, text-to-speech, OCR, and transliteration across 22 Indian languages, BHASHINI has achieved 5 billion+ AI inferences nationally. The My Aadhaar identity service alone recorded 1.2 billion+ inferences, while eGramSwaraj generated 455 million API calls supporting Panchayat-level governance. By making government services voice-first and multilingual, BHASHINI addresses deep linguistic barriers that previously excluded rural and regional populations from digital public communication.
details:
The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) is a national initiative of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, implemented under the National Language Translation Mission. Launched in 2022 as part of the Digital India programme, BHASHINI (Bhasha Interface for India) positions language as core digital infrastructure, enabling citizens to access public information and services in the languages they speak and understand.

BHASHINI functions as a voice-first, multimodal AI ecosystem, offering shared language infrastructure for governance and public communication. It provides 18+ AI-powered services including Machine Translation, Speech-to-Speech Translation, Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Text-to-Speech (TTS), Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Transliteration, and advanced pre- and post-processing tools such as language detection, denoising, punctuation and voice activity detection. These capabilities are delivered through open, interoperable APIs and support 36+ Indian languages for text and 22+ Indian languages for voice, enabling real-time multilingual interaction across text, voice, image and video.

BHASHINI’s target audience includes citizens with limited literacy or English proficiency, public institutions, developers, startups, and academic partners. The BHASHINI Mobile App extends these services directly to citizens, supporting real-world language access beyond institutional platforms. Community-driven initiatives such as BhashaDaan and BHASHINI Samudaye ensure that datasets, glossaries and language models are shaped by diverse linguistic communities.

As of 2025, BHASHINI has delivered over 5 billion AI inferences, enabled 1.1 million+ mobile app downloads, translated 400+ government websites, supported 100+ use cases across sectors, and facilitated access for over 100 crore Indians, including farmers, students, women, elderly citizens and low-literacy populations. The World Economic Forum has highlighted BHASHINI as a global example of inclusive, open digital public infrastructure. Its innovation lies in institutionalising multilingual AI as shared national infrastructure, rather than isolated tools, ensuring clarity, inclusion and trust in public communication at scale."BHASHINI is embedded within India’s public policy architecture through the National Language Translation Mission, aligned with the Digital India and IndiaAI missions. It operationalises constitutional commitments to linguistic inclusion by integrating multilingual and voice-enabled communication directly into public digital systems.
The platform is formally adopted by multiple Central Ministries, State Governments and public institutions across governance, identity, transport, health, education, finance, skilling and grievance redressal. Key integrations include My Aadhaar, eGramSwaraj, Indian Railways (Rail Madad), CPGRAMS, PM-Kisan, POSHAN Tracker, DIKSHA, Janaushadhi, MGNREGA systems, and Panchayat platforms.
A flagship governance innovation is SabhaSaar, which uses BHASHINI to automatically generate multilingual Gram Sabha minutes, strengthening transparency and participation in local democracy. BHASHINI’s institutional design enables ministries to adopt a common language layer, ensuring consistency, scalability and interoperability across public services while reducing duplication of effort."

name: Weaving the Web of Truth: MEC’s Multi-Platform Campaign on Voter Education and Countering  Disinformation
desc: Weaving the Web of Truth was Malawi Electoral Commission's multi-platform voter education campaign during the 2025 General Election. Responding to growing disinformation and political polarization, MEC integrated community engagement, mass media, digital platforms, and assistive technologies into a unified communication model. At grassroots level, 229 Constituency Civic Education Assistants conducted village meetings and dialogues. The campaign generated 9,450+ radio and TV broadcast slots and 15.8 million online interactions. Voter turnout rose from 64.8% in 2020 to 76.4% in 2025—one of the largest increases in recent Malawian elections—demonstrating that coordinated, inclusive public communication directly strengthens democratic participation.
details:
"During 2025 General Election, MEC implemented a communication campaign aimed at increasing voter turnout, countering disinformation, & strengthening trust in elections. This initiative responded to a challenging context marked by rapid growth of online disinformation, political polarization, skepticism toward new electoral technologies, and absence of CSO in voter education.

MEC adopted a communication model that integrated community engagement, mass media, digital platforms, assistive technologies, and direct stakeholder networks into a single “web of truth.” The campaign targeted all eligible voters: youth, women, persons with disabilities, rural communities, political actors, media, traditional & faith leaders with messages tailored to their specific information needs.

At grassroots level,  229 Constituency Civic and Voter Education Assistants conducted village meetings, door-to-door outreach, market sensitization, youth and women dialogues, and engagements with religious institutions. They also practiced active listening, feeding community concerns back to MEC to inform real-time message adjustment. CCVEAs acted as frontline defenders against rumor-based, word-of-mouth disinformation.

To reach populations with limited access to digital or broadcast media, MEC deployed loudhailers and mobile public address systems broadcasting messages in local languages.

MEC rolled out an extensive radio and television campaign using PSAs, jingles, dramas, talk shows, phone-ins, and live interviews. All major TV appearances included sign language interpretation, institutionalizing accessibility.

MEC expanded its social media presence with daily updates, infographics, explainer videos, live-streamed briefings, and a structured 300-day countdown to polling day. MEC established WhatsApp groups for political parties and candidates and maintained an email mailing list of over 6,000 active addresses to ensure direct, consistent information flow to stakeholders.

MEC invested in social media monitoring. Detected false or misleading content triggered immediate verification and rapid release of corrective messages across all channels. This functioned as an “information iron dome,” enabling MEC’s truthful messages to outpace, intercept, and often reverse fake news.

Partnerships with influencers acted as information multipliers by amplifying MEC content and as sentinels by cross-checking rumors before sharing and alerting MEC to emerging narratives.

MEC implemented Open National Tally Centre with live-streamed tallying and unrestricted access.

The impact was tangible: recorded a voter turnout of 76.4%, the highest in recent history. Stakeholders commended MEC’s transparency, responsiveness, inclusivity, and professionalism. The initiative is innovative because it redefines public communication as an integrated ecosystem that floods the information environment with credible, accessible truth from many directions, making disinformation difficult to survive." "This initiative is grounded in MEC's constitutional mandate and its 2023–2028 Strategic Plan, which recognizes communication and voter education as central pillars of credible elections. The Commission is legally required to provide voter education, disseminate electoral information, strengthen stakeholder engagement, promote transparency, and build public confidence in electoral processes. The multi-channel communication campaign directly operationalized these statutory obligations at national scale.

The 2025 communication model also advances Malawi 2063, particularly Enabler 2: Effective Governance Systems and Institutions. By prioritizing transparency, accessibility, inclusion, digital engagement, and two-way communication, the initiative strengthened governance practices, reinforced the rule of law, and expanded meaningful citizen participation. Citizens were empowered to access information, exercise their rights, articulate concerns, and engage constructively with the electoral process, thereby contributing to accountable and responsive institutions.

In addition, the initiative aligns with electoral laws, the Access to Information Act, and regional and continental democratic frameworks of SADC and AU. Components such as constituency-based field educators, mass media programming, livestreamed electoral processes, disability-inclusive communication, and direct stakeholder communication networks translate public policy commitments into daily institutional practice.
"

desc: Les Ondes de la Parole Publique (The Waves of Public Speech) by the Faculty of Legal and Political Sciences at the University of Bangui in the Central African Republic aims to transform public communication into a living, comprehensible, inclusive flow that restores trust between institutions and citizens. Recognizing that public messages often remain opaque—generating incomprehension, disengagement, and rumors—the initiative creates resonance spaces where citizens can ask questions and share reactions, and establishes feedback loops enabling institutions to improve their communication. Currently in conceptual and pilot design phase, it establishes a methodologically rigorous framework for participatory public communication in the Central African Republic.
details:
"The Waves of Public Speech is an initiative aimed at transforming public communication into a vibrant, understandable, and inclusive flow, capable of restoring trust between institutions and citizens. In many contexts, public messages remain opaque: decisions, programs, and policies circulate without being truly understood, generating misunderstanding, disengagement, and rumors.

This initiative stems from this observation and places clarity, listening, and participation at the heart of public communication.

The main objective is to make every message accessible and appropriable by everyone, especially young people and traditionally underrepresented groups. The initiative creates spaces for dialogue, where citizens can ask questions and share their reactions, and establishes feedback loops that allow institutions to reformulate and improve their communication. The stakeholders involved include national and local public institutions, civil society organizations, and media partners, working together to strengthen participation and inclusion.

The innovation of this initiative lies in its systemic vision of communication: it is not limited to the dissemination of messages, but follows their journeys." The initiative tracks the actual trajectory, identifies where misunderstandings occur, and continuously adjusts the flow. This approach transforms public communication into an active and ethical dialogue, where discourse doesn't tower over citizens but circulates with them. It illustrates how governance can become tangible, experienced, and understandable to all, without relying on sophisticated technological tools. By fostering clarity, inclusion, and dialogue, the initiative contributes to a more participatory democracy and a lasting relationship of trust between institutions and the public.The "Waves of Public Discourse" initiative is directly aligned with the missions of public communication and governance institutions, particularly those responsible for disseminating decisions, programs, and public policies. The initiative collaborates with national and local administrations to improve how their messages are received and understood by citizens. It complements existing public policies on transparency, citizen participation, and inclusion by creating mechanisms for concrete and continuous feedback between institutions and the public. By establishing spaces for dialogue and feedback loops, it strengthens the reach and effectiveness of public policies, especially those concerning young people, marginalized communities, and areas often overlooked by official channels.

The initiative's innovation lies in viewing communication not as a one-off institutional obligation, but as a strategic governance tool capable of strengthening trust and citizen participation, and of making public decisions tangible, understandable, and accessible to all.

name: Sistema Mendocino de Comunicación Pública Basada en Evidencia (SIMECPE)
desc: SIMECPE (Mendoza Evidence-Based Public Communication System) by RZ Consultora in Argentina integrates academic research, public opinion surveys, and strategic analysis to improve institutional communication in polarized contexts. Born in Mendoza province, it combines a master's research study on leadership in fragmented party systems, citizen surveys on political sentiment, and tools for understanding collective social emotions. Its surveys—'Post-Electoral Sentiment' and 'Power and Leadership in Mendoza'—were disseminated across regional television, radio, and digital media, generating public debates grounded in verifiable data. SIMECPE offers institutions a methodology for evidence-based communication that builds credibility in polarized democratic environments.
details:
The Mendoza System of Evidence-Based Public Communication (SIMECPE) is an initiative that integrates academic research, opinion polls, and strategic analysis to improve public communication in contexts of polarization and crisis of representation. It originated in the province of Mendoza, Argentina, with the goal of strengthening the relationship between institutions and citizens through clear information, evidence-based dialogue, and a deep understanding of contemporary social emotions.

The initiative comprises three core components.
The first is a master's thesis on dominant leadership in broken party systems (2022–2025), which analyzes how political discourses construct legitimacy, crisis narratives, and affective bonds with society. This study offers a solid conceptual framework for understanding how emotions, political myth, and the politics of risk influence public perception and institutional decision-making.

The second and third components consist of two public opinion polls conducted in Mendoza: “Post-Electoral Sentiment” and “Power and Leadership in Mendoza.” The first measures social emotions. (hope, anger, uncertainty), institutional trust, and citizen expectations after electoral processes. The second analyzes leadership preferences, demands for political leadership, the evaluation of social actors (universities, civil society, the private sector), and perceptions of political renewal.

These three inputs are combined in a system that produces accessible reports, clear narratives, and practical recommendations for public institutions, government communicators, open government agencies, journalists, and technical teams. The goal is to translate complex phenomena—polarization, crisis of representation, social emotions, and perceptions of leadership—into understandable and actionable information.

The initiative is innovative because it integrates quantitative evidence, qualitative analysis, and narrative construction into a single tool applied to public communication. It does not simply describe data: it interprets it, translates it into communicational terms, and proposes strategies to improve social dialogue and reduce symbolic confrontation. Furthermore, it addresses the gap between politics, citizenship, and communication management through an interdisciplinary approach that combines political science, discourse analysis, the sociology of emotions, and government communication.

SIMECPE identifies polarization risks, emerging patterns of distrust, leadership preferences, and social demands. Based on this, it generates recommendations for ethical, empathetic public communication oriented towards the collective interest. The initiative is replicable in any province or municipality in Latin America facing similar challenges." The SIMECPE initiative is directly linked to public institutions and decision-making processes in the province of Mendoza. First, the project provides strategic support to government departments within the Mendoza government, particularly in areas such as institutional communication, public perception, security, health, water, and public services. Opinion polls and discourse analysis have been used by technical teams to refine messaging, improve communication of public policies, and guide local interventions.

name: Ancla de Voces de Chinú
org: Asociacion Comunitaria de Comunicacion Social Municipio de Chinu
desc: Ancla de Voces de Chinú is a community communication model led by Caribe Stereo community radio in Chinú, Córdoba, Colombia. The initiative addresses communication gaps and low digital literacy by transforming complex public information into active dialogue through three phases: radio micro-podcasts simplifying public policies, a network of trained community 'anchors' distributing information door-to-door offline, and WhatsApp channels collecting citizen feedback. This hybrid of traditional radio, human networks, and accessible mobile technology creates a closed-loop information system particularly effective in rural and low-connectivity communities where digital platforms alone fail to reach residents.
details:
Summary: Chinú Voices Anchor (AVC) - Innovation in Community Communication

The Chinú Voices Anchor (AVC) initiative, led by the community radio station Caribe Stereo, is a disruptive model that addresses the communication gap and low digital literacy in Chinú, Córdoba, by transforming complex information into active dialogue. Its innovation lies in the strategic combination of traditional media, human participation, and user-friendly mobile technology.

The Innovative Mechanism: From Radio to the Field

AVC operates as a closed-loop information and listening system in three key phases:

1. Caribe Capsules (Clarity in Action): The station simplifies public policies (e.g., agricultural subsidies, requirements for formalizing footwear production) into 2-3 minute micro-podcasts. This content is designed to be concise and educational.

2. The Community Anchors Network (Inclusive Voices / Offline Distribution): This is the cornerstone of innovation. Caribe Stereo trains a network of "Community Anchors" (young people and neighborhood leaders) who act as emissaries. Equipped with portable speakers, they distribute the capsules offline in rural areas, farms, and groups of shoe producers where radio or internet signal is nonexistent ("last mile"). This ensures that vital information reaches senior citizens and rural communities.

3. Active Listening with WhatsApp (Exploring New Frontiers): The Anchors use Caribe Stereo's WhatsApp number, 3016269022, to capture citizens' questions, doubts, and complaints in voice message format. This method preserves the authentic tone of the citizen's voice and facilitates the participation of people who cannot write.

Closing the Cycle and Transparency: The station uses these captured voices to generate new weekly Caribe Capsules, dedicated exclusively to providing direct and institutional answers to questions. This transforms Caribe Stereo into a mechanism for institutional active listening that generates a cycle of trust and transparency. demonstrating that the local government is responding to the genuine needs of the community." "Linkage with Public Policies or Institutions
Key Implementer: Caribe Stereo Community Radio Station (Public Media Outlet).
Institutional Collaborators:
Chinú Municipality (Social Development Office): Provides technical information on programs (e.g., subsidies for agricultural inputs, vaccination campaigns) to be translated into Caribe Capsules.
Footwear Artisans Guild (ASOCALCE): The radio station is directly linked to local economic development policies, creating specific capsules on trade regulations, combating smuggling, and design trends (such as the AI ​​mentioned by artisan Jurado).
Transparency and Participation Policies: The RVA serves as the inclusive communication arm of transparency policies, providing evidence that information is disseminated even to the most vulnerable groups, and that their voices are heard and responded to by the local government."

name: VALUEbot : Una plataforma generadora de chatbots mediante IA para la comunicación del valor público del PSM
org: Universidad Santiago de Compostela . Facultad de Ciencias de la  Comunicación
desc: VALUEbot is an AI-powered chatbot generation platform developed by the University of Santiago de Compostela since 2023, transforming complex institutional documents, strategies, and materials into accessible conversations. Its modular architecture supports both cloud-based and local AI models, offering technological independence and privacy protection. The platform has accumulated approximately 1,000 conversation records through professional testing. Tested by Galician public media (CRTVG, CMM) and used by the CIRCOM Chair at Universidad de Vigo to disseminate reports conversationally, VALUEbot offers a privacy-respecting institutional solution for transforming dense public information into citizen-friendly dialogue.
details:
VALUEbot is an initiative designed to transform complex documents, strategies, and materials into accessible conversations using an AI-powered chatbot platform. Since 2023, the project has been developing an infrastructure designed for contexts where information overload and fragmentation make it difficult for citizens to access clear and understandable information. Its design aims to transform institutional content into structured dialogue with stylistic consistency, traceability, and the ability to explain values, objectives, and decisions.

The initiative incorporates a modular architecture that allows working with both cloud-based AI models and pre-trained local engines, offering technological independence from large platforms, enhanced privacy, and control over data flows. This flexibility allows the tool to be adapted to different levels of technical requirements and ensures that organizations maintain sovereignty over the information they use. VALUEbot also integrates an operational ethics matrix that guides conversational behavior and ensures that each response aligns with social values ​​and criteria of clarity and respect.

Its target audience includes communication professionals, educators, and community groups. Social groups and individuals who need direct and understandable access to complex information. The project has been explicitly opened to organizations and community groups through an open-source approach, allowing each group to adapt the tool to their needs and generate their own conversational assistants without depending on external providers. This openness seeks to foster technological ownership, reduce barriers to entry, and facilitate autonomous use in diverse contexts.

The system's development follows an iterative process based on Participatory Action Research and User-Centered Design, with the participation of public communication specialists, interaction designers, technical teams, and researchers who contribute to refining prototypes and ensuring coherence between usability, accessibility, and ethical principles. Its innovative nature lies in combining local AI, traceability, integrated values, and community openness to enable clear, responsible, and adaptable conversational communication.

VALUEbot maintains a direct link with public institutions and with policies aimed at innovation, inclusion and modernization of public communication. Its development is articulated within the PSMresearchTeam of the Universidade de Santiago de Compostela, in a collaborative process that brings together multiple actors from the public audiovisual field, such as CRTVG, CMM, Canal Sur and the Finnish radio and television station YLE, together with professionals from the Dutch public television NPO. These entities participated in interviews, discussion groups and technical validations that made it possible to define functionalities, ethical criteria and real public communication needs in different European contexts. The project integrates the collaboration of universities with experience in media governance and innovation, such as the University of Tampere and the Media and Journalism Research Center (MJRC), whose contributions strengthen the academic and methodological fit in inclusive public communication policies. Thanks to these alliances, VALUEbot aligns itself with policies of responsible digitalization, transparency and improvement of communicative accessibility. VALUEbot uses local AI to ensure independence, protect privacy, integrating an ethical matrix. All of this coincides with the guidelines of the UNDP Atlas, which promotes innovations capable of amplifying voices, facilitating public understanding and connecting citizens and institutions through safe and socially responsible technologies.

name: Elvia Derechos
org: Instituto Electoral y de Participación Ciudadana de Yucatán
desc: Elvia Derechos is a digital AI-powered platform by the Electoral Institute of Yucatán, Mexico, facilitating access to political-electoral rights. Named after pioneer Elvia Carrillo Puerto, the platform uses an AI agent trained exclusively on electoral legislation, jurisdictional criteria, and official protocols to provide practical, actionable guidance on running for office, accessing candidacies, presenting complaints, and using legal challenge procedures. The platform stores no personal data, guaranteeing privacy. Following its launch, Elvia Derechos received national media coverage on Telesur, Canal 13, Teleplay, and major radio stations—demonstrating significant public interest in accessible electoral rights communication tools.
details:
“‘Elvia Derechos’ is an accessible digital platform that facilitates the exercise and defense of political and electoral rights in Yucatán. It uses artificial intelligence trained exclusively on local and federal legislation, jurisdictional criteria, official protocols, and documented best practices, reducing misinformation and bringing citizens closer to justice and democratic participation. Its name honors Elvia Carrillo Puerto, a pioneer in women’s political rights.

This conversational agent offers practical and actionable guidance on how to participate in public decisions, hold office without violence, access a candidacy, or file complaints, reports, and appeals. It explains deadlines and requirements, simplifies legal procedures, and provides verified contacts for the relevant authorities. The site does not store personal data, guaranteeing privacy and security.

The target audience includes women, youth, Indigenous people, the LGBTIQ+ community, people with disabilities, party members, and public officials. The tool operates 24/7 at elviaderechos.com and integrates WhatsApp and SMS channels, expanding its reach to people with Low connectivity.

The initiative was launched on November 25, 2025, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, and was developed by an interdisciplinary team from the IEPAC (Electoral and Citizen Participation Institute of Yucatán) with expertise in electoral law, communication, and technology. Civil society organizations and activists participated from the early stages, providing expert feedback.

'Elvia Derechos' innovates by combining specialized AI, accessible language, and a rights-based approach to democratize public information and close gaps in access to electoral justice and citizen participation mechanisms. Its modular architecture allows the model to be replicated in other entities, strengthening the relationship between citizens and institutions through inclusive, verifiable, and transparent information.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u52mq33qFVM "Elvia Derechos" emerged within the Electoral and Citizen Participation Institute of Yucatán (IEPAC) in response to the lack of a public defender's office for political and electoral rights. Although the State Congress approved Decree 655/2023 to create one, it was never implemented due to budget constraints and internal resistance, leaving Yucatán as one of the few states in the country without a public mechanism for guidance on this matter.

Faced with this void, the IEPAC identified the urgent need to provide citizens with clear information about their political and electoral rights, the available institutional channels, and the competent authority for each type of conflict. Based on its mandate in civic education, citizen participation, substantive equality, and the prevention of political violence, the Institute developed an immediate and accessible alternative: "Elvia Derechos," a digital platform that translates the legal and electoral framework into understandable and actionable guidance.

The initiative is directly linked to public policies on access to justice, democratic strengthening, and the guarantee of political and electoral rights. Although it does not replace the ombudsman's office provided for by law, it temporarily fills the gap, providing a reliable, timely channel aligned with the institutional mandate to ensure that citizens can exercise their rights without barriers."
