name: ECOS DE CIENAGA ORO
desc: Ecos de Ciénaga de Oro is a community radio and citizen dialogue initiative by Latina Stereo 89.0FM in Ciénaga de Oro, Colombia. Using radio gamification and Participatory Community Audio (ACP), it transforms complex topics—ecosystem protection, local history, cultural regulation—into accessible interactive experiences. Citizens send audio responses and historical data via chat tools, which are broadcast and distributed through WhatsApp, Facebook, and Telegram. This methodology validates oral memory as a primary knowledge source, fostering intergenerational active listening and strengthening community trust in cultural institutions. Since its 2024 launch, the initiative has maintained sustained multi-generational participation.
details:
"Initiative Summary

Ecos de Ciénaga de Oro is a public communication and citizen dialogue initiative designed to transform complex topics (such as ecosystem protection, local history, and cultural regulations) into interactive and accessible experiences. The initiative is based on radio gamification through a weekly segment on Latina Stereo. It utilizes Participatory Community Audio (PCA), where citizens are invited to record short responses, anecdotes, or historical facts about Ciénaga de Oro using audio chat tools, disseminating all the material through the website (Facebook, WhatsApp). This method guarantees Active Listening and Intergenerational Dialogue by recovering and validating local Oral History as a primary source of knowledge, strengthening trust in the institutions that support this cultural recovery.

Initiative Objectives

To translate complex topics (ecosystem protection, local history, cultural regulations) into accessible communicative experiences for everyone community.

Promote citizen participation through the use of Participatory Community Audio (PCA), inviting people to contribute local knowledge, anecdotes, and memories.
Strengthen active listening and intergenerational dialogue, recognizing and validating Oral History as a legitimate source of knowledge.
Increase community trust in the institutions involved in cultural preservation and public communication.
Expand access to local information through multiplatform strategies (radio, Telegram, Facebook, WhatsApp, web).

Target audience

Residents of Ciénaga de Oro, especially those with historical, cultural, or environmental knowledge.
Older adults who are bearers of oral history.
Youth and adolescents, to foster generational renewal and the use of innovative formats.
The general community interested in local identity, culture, and heritage.
Key community stakeholders (leaders, teachers, cultural managers).

Year of development

The initiative was developed in 2024.

The initiative is innovative because It combines traditional radio with gamification and the use of Participatory Community Audio, allowing any citizen to generate content and become a primary source of knowledge. By integrating oral history, intergenerational participation, and accessible digital platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, and Facebook, it creates a unique communication ecosystem that transforms complex issues into relatable and collaborative experiences. This blend of simple technology, citizen dialogue, and cultural recovery makes “Ecos de Ciénaga de Oro” a novel model of public communication and local knowledge management. "Ecos de Ciénaga de Oro is directly linked to the municipality's cultural and environmental public policies by contributing to the safeguarding of intangible heritage and community education. Its focus on recovering oral history strengthens the institutional objectives of preserving local identity, documenting traditional knowledge, and promoting citizen participation in knowledge building. Through its partnership with the community radio station Latina Stereo and coordinated work with local cultural and environmental agencies, the initiative offers an effective channel for institutions to disseminate information, gather citizen input, and connect their programs with the realities of the region.

The Participatory Community Audio methodology also aligns with transparency and governance policies by creating spaces where the community interacts horizontally with public actors. This active listening process informs institutional decisions and strengthens trust in the entities that support cultural recovery. Thus, the initiative acts as a bridge between citizens and institutions, facilitating the implementation and social appropriation of local public policies."

name: Minha Escola Ensina Direitos
org: Defensoria Pública do Estado do Ceará
desc: Minha Escola Ensina Direitos is a project by Ceará's Public Defender's Office promoting children's and adolescents' rights in public schools using plain language materials. Now in its second consecutive year, the initiative brings rights-based discussions into classrooms through a monthly binder workbook, folders, and banners, with two public defenders visiting each school monthly. A creative competition at year's end reinforces learning. In 2025, the program reached 280 students across 5 cities and won first place in the popular vote at the 2nd Plain Language Marathon for Citizenship—organized by the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies' Hacker Lab—validating it as a national reference for accessible institutional communication.
details: My School Teaches Rights is a project to promote the rights of children and adolescents in 14 public schools across 3 cities. It's in its second consecutive year and aims to bring discussions that go beyond textbooks into the classroom, contributing to the full exercise of citizenship. Within this scope, the Communications Department (Secom) was tasked with developing all the didactic content and visual identity of the project, starting with the program's name. Our proposal was to create visually appealing and easily understandable material using simple language. A binder-style notebook was prepared, separating the themes by month, and printed in a thousand copies. In addition, brochures and banners were used to publicize the monthly activities at the school, where two advocates address the defined themes. At the end of the year, Secom organized a contest of activities for the students based on the content learned. The simple language approach was designed to ensure that young people understand the information and exercise their citizenship, without language being an obstacle to accessing their rights. In addition to democratizing knowledge about rights, the initiative fosters youth empowerment, encouraging debate and participation in practical activities.

name: Personaliza.br
desc: Personaliza.br is Brazil's new personalized public communication architecture led by the Secretariat of Digital Government. Its centerpiece is the Caixa Postal Digital—a free, protected official channel within the gov.br platform automatically available to over 164 million Brazilians. The ecosystem integrates notifications via Caixa Postal, app push notifications, and official messages through WhatsApp, SMS, RCS, and authenticated email—always linked to public services and citizen rights. Since 2025, the system has sent over 140 million messages, with the Caixa Postal achieving a 15% average read rate (exceeding traditional email/SMS benchmarks) and 95% satisfaction rate—making it Brazil's primary personalized government communication channel.
details:
"The Personaliza Gov initiative, including the Citizen's Digital Mailbox, led by the Secretariat of Digital Government (Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services), is the new architecture for personalized public communication of the Federal Government. Its objective is to make state communication more secure, useful, inclusive, and relevant, anticipating citizens' needs and reducing noise, fraud, and misinformation.

Launched in 2025, the Mailbox is an official, free, and protected channel within the gov.br platform, automatically available to more than 164 million people. The initiative consolidates an integrated public communication ecosystem that includes personalized notifications via Mailbox, push notifications in the gov.br app, and official messages via WhatsApp, SMS, RCS, and authenticated email – always linked to public services, public policies, and citizens' rights.

The central motivation is the contemporary challenge described by the UNDP Atlas: how to communicate clearly, reliably, and inclusively in an environment of information overload and increased fraud. While emails and SMS are widely exploited by spammers and..." To combat fraud, the Mailbox creates a secure and noise-free environment, accessible through a validated digital identity (Silver and Gold levels).

The initiative involves public actors from across the Federal Government, including sectoral ministries (Education, Labor, Health, Justice, among others) and state agencies such as the Federal Revenue Service and INSS (National Institute of Social Security). These partners use Personaliza Gov to send reliable notifications about benefits, obligations, educational opportunities, document expirations, and security alerts.

The system uses segmentation based on data intelligence and simple language patterns, ensuring that each citizen receives only messages relevant to their profile and life stage. Simultaneously, educational campaigns reinforce good digital security practices, reducing phishing risks and increasing trust in official channels.

The innovation of the initiative lies in the unprecedented combination of personalization, security, multichannel integration, identity verification, and simple language, with metrics on readability, reach, and effectiveness.

The result is a new standard of active, preventive, and citizen-centered public communication, transforming gov.br from a passive portal into a proactive care system. Guidance and protection, aligned with the dimensions of trust, inclusion, and innovation highlighted by the UNDP Atlas."

name: Campanha “O cuidado não pode ficar só no off” - Defesa dos Direitos de Crianças e Adolescentes no ambiente digital.
org: Ministério Público do Estado da Bahia (MPBA).
desc: The campaign 'O Cuidado Não Pode Ficar Só no Off' (Caring Can't Stay Offline) is an integrated communication initiative by Bahia's Public Ministry to mobilize parents and guardians on digital violence prevention for children and adolescents. The initiative combines a multi-channel advertising campaign with the Fala Filho platform—an AI-powered tool providing empathetic responses to parents' questions about online risks—plus a pedagogical manual and media partners across Bahia. Between October and November 2025, the Fala Filho platform recorded significant uptake from parents seeking guidance on children's internet safety, validating AI-assisted public communication as a scalable child protection outreach tool.
details:
"The integrated communication action, an initiative of the Public Prosecutor's Office of Bahia's Center for Operational Support for Children and Adolescents (Caoca) and executed through the Social Communication Coordination of the MPBA, has as its central objective to sensitize, guide, and mobilize parents, guardians, and society in general for the prevention and confrontation of violence in the digital environment, disseminating qualified information, promoting the integral protection of children and adolescents, and strengthening the role of the MPBA as an agent for the promotion of rights and education for digital citizenship.

The initiative is composed of several fronts:
- Advertising campaign with pieces, media, and partners from Bahia and even from outside the State, since it was replicated by other units of the Public Prosecutor's Office.
- The Fala Filho digital platform: uses artificial intelligence to answer, in a simple and empathetic way, the main questions of parents and guardians about risks on the internet. The answers are presented by digital avatars that represent children and adolescents, promoting clarifying conversations and valuing the protagonism of children and youth. To access, simply visit the website." falafilho.com.br, specify the age range and choose the avatar that represents the child or adolescent you wish to protect. The platform, with youthful and accessible language, provides guidance on types of digital violence, warning signs, safe internet use, and also offers information on legislation, reporting channels, and forms of support and emotional assistance.

- Press Office: responsible for disseminating the campaign among media outlets.

- Guerrilla Action: carried out in schools with parents and guardians, generating videos for digital platforms and expanding the reach of the message.

The target audience of the campaign, developed between July and October 2025, includes parents and guardians of children and adolescents, education and health professionals, families, and society in general. Dissemination began on October 18, 2025.

The MPBA campaign constituted an innovative public communication action by strategically and uniquely integrating different fronts of social mobilization. The initiative articulated press relations, its own digital platform that offers continuous guidance to Parents and guardians (www.falafilho.com.br), in-person outreach activities with parents and guardians in schools, and the voluntary participation of the artist Lore Improta, expanding reach and engagement. This multi-channel approach, centered on the citizen and oriented towards prevention, consolidated a contemporary, integrated, accessible, effective public communication, focused on the citizen and oriented towards behavior change, capable of transforming information into protection and strengthening the institutional role of the MPBA (Public Prosecutor's Office of Bahia) in promoting rights. It combined digital communication, territorial presence, and social influence.

Partners, among others: Morya Comunicação Agency

name: Simplificação e acessibilidade em perguntas e respostas sobre esporotricose e covid-19
org: Instituto de Comunicação e Informação Científica e Tecnológica em Saúde (Icict/Fiocruz)
desc: The FAQ simplification initiative at Fiocruz's Portal reorganized and rewrote Q&A pages on health conditions including sporotrichosis and COVID-19 using plain language principles. Guided by analysis showing disease-related content was the most accessed on the portal, the team produced simplified, accessible answers co-developed with medical specialists. The 2022 rewrite of the sporotrichosis FAQ—a disease affecting vulnerable urban populations—demonstrated measurable comprehension improvement. Part of a broader Fiocruz plain language programme, this initiative establishes the institution as a national reference for accessible science communication in Brazilian public health.
details:
"The Oswaldo Cruz Foundation (Fiocruz) is one of Brazil's leading public health institutions. Its work encompasses the production, dissemination, and sharing of knowledge and technologies that strengthen the Unified Health System (SUS), promote health and quality of life, reduce social inequalities, and drive innovation in the country, with the defense of the right to health and citizenship as its central values. Among the institution's actions, the public communication of science on health topics stands out, seeking to present content in an accessible and understandable way.

In this context, the Fiocruz Portal, coordinated by the Institute of Scientific and Technological Communication and Information in Health (Icict/Fiocruz), is consolidated as an important channel for disseminating this information. Based on an analysis of historical data on portal access, we observed that articles dealing with diseases, their causes, and treatments were the most accessed by the public over the years. Therefore, we created Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) pages on different diseases to facilitate access to this information." Through direct and simplified content.

In our work, the pages on sporotrichosis and COVID-19 stand out for several reasons. Sporotrichosis is a fungal disease that is quite common in Rio de Janeiro, both in rural and urban areas, transmitted through contaminated soil or contact with infected cats. In addition to creating the questions and answers to facilitate the flow of information, we simplified the text and translated it into Libras (Brazilian Sign Language) in 2022 to ensure comprehension by people with low literacy and/or who are deaf. The Q&A on COVID-19 was published on the portal in 2020 during the pandemic. Besides simplifying the text, we created an online poll alongside each published piece of content to assess citizen opinion, asking if they had found what they were looking for, if they had understood the information, and if they considered the content up-to-date. With this feedback, we were able to assess, in real time, whether any question was outdated or confusing for the citizen and needed further revision or simplification. Based on other Q&A pages, we verified that these solutions were innovative at the time of their implementation, as we did not identify similar alternatives. This experience demonstrated that simplifying language, promoting accessibility, and allowing citizen participation in content evaluation contribute significantly to democratizing access to health information.

name: Rede InovaGov
desc: Rede InovaGov (InnovaGov Network) by Brazil's National School of Public Administration (Enap) is a collaborative ecosystem transforming public communication into a distributed, participatory practice. Connecting 13,000+ members from federal, state, and municipal agencies, universities, and collectives, the network operates through 22 communities of practice, 40+ WhatsApp thematic groups, an open digital platform, and a collaborative library. Any member can participate and propose content regardless of their organization. By December 2025, the platform had 82 innovation units and 102 mapped initiatives—demonstrating how horizontal communication architecture can build innovation culture across fragmented public administration ecosystems.
details:
"The InovaGov Network is a collaborative ecosystem coordinated by the National School of Public Administration (Enap) that transforms public communication into a distributed, participatory practice oriented towards government innovation. Created to connect people and institutions working with innovation in the public sector, the network brings together more than 13,000 members from federal, state, and municipal agencies, as well as universities, partner organizations, and independent collectives.
Its objective is to facilitate the circulation of knowledge, support capacity building, and strengthen collaboration between institutions through a horizontal communication architecture. The network operates through 22 communities of practice, more than 40 thematic groups on WhatsApp, an open digital platform, a collaborative library, newsletters, and a collectively built monthly agenda. This structure allows anyone—regardless of their originating agency—to participate, propose content, and co-curate practices, expanding access to government innovation.
One of the most innovative elements of the initiative is the InovaGov Experience, the network's official space during Enap's Innovation Week. The curation is entirely horizontal: community leaders and network members propose..." The activities and programming are built in an open and participatory way. This transforms Innovation Week into an annual showcase of distributed public communication, revealing projects, narratives, and learnings produced collectively throughout the year.
Another distinguishing feature is the autonomy of the communities. Several initiatives emerge spontaneously — events, methodologies, discussion groups, shared materials — without direct intervention from Enap. Starting in 2026, the network will begin a mentoring cycle to support leaders in the design, communication, and sustainability of these projects, consolidating new capabilities and strengthening the continuity of the ecosystem.

The InovaGov Network is innovative because it breaks with the traditional model of public communication based on centralized broadcasts. By combining low-cost social technologies, distributed channels, and collaborative practices, it transforms communication into articulation, articulation into dialogue, and dialogue into collective action. The result is a living network that amplifies the voice of public servants, accelerates the circulation of good practices, and strengthens public innovation in the country.

name: A Câmara do Rio na Rua
org: Câmara Municipal do Rio de Janeiro
desc: A Câmara do Rio na Rua (Rio Council in the Streets) is a civic engagement initiative of Rio de Janeiro's Municipal Chamber comprising three projects: O Povo Pergunta, Extra Favelas, and Praça da Cidadania. The initiative's innovation lies in decentralization—bringing legislative activity to public spaces for direct, face-to-face citizen dialogue. O Povo Pergunta combines in-person encounters in high-traffic areas with radio broadcasts; Extra Favelas brings community debates inside favelas; Praça da Cidadania holds civic events in public squares. Together, they reframe transparency and participation as concrete tools for building fairer public policies, generating broad media coverage and positive testimonials from diverse participant groups.
details:
"The initiative of the Rio de Janeiro City Council, comprised of the projects “The People Ask,” “Extra Favelas,” and “Citizenship Square,” constitutes an innovative and replicable model of civic engagement. Its main innovative strength lies in the decentralization and horizontality of the relationship between the Public Power and the population, taking the City Council to the streets to promote active listening and face-to-face dialogue. This approach redefines transparency and participation, transforming them into concrete tools for building fairer and more effective state policies.
The innovation is detailed in each component:
The “The People Ask” project innovates through its multi-channel approach, integrating face-to-face dialogue in high-traffic locations (such as terminals and pedestrian walkways) with the broad visibility of radio (traditional media). This combination decentralizes legislative activity and creates a forum for direct and immediate contact with citizens, reinforcing the commitment to the city and making the work of the City Council more transparent.
The action consistently promotes a direct, transparent, and responsive relationship between the Public Power and the population." Legislative branch and the population. By bringing council members to speak face-to-face with citizens in different neighborhoods of the city, the project breaks down institutional barriers and creates an environment of open dialogue, where criticisms, demands, and suggestions are received directly. This format demonstrates a willingness to listen, learn, and adjust priorities based on the reality of the residents, strengthening the credibility of the City Council.
The “Extra Favelas” debate cycle represents a powerful form of social and methodological innovation. The project establishes a direct and structured channel with favela communities in all regions of the city, giving voice to historically marginalized groups. The central innovation is to use a hybrid model (face-to-face thematic debates combined with research) to ensure that public policies are built from the “peripheral perspective” of those who live in the territories.
The “Citizenship Square” innovates by overcoming the physical and psychological barrier of the Legislative Palace. It condenses the entire structure of the Legislative branch (councilors, staff, and the 28 Permanent Committees) in a single external location.

The initiative also It innovated by integrating in-person service with digital civic education, introducing an interactive panel to educate citizens on how to use the Chamber's website to suggest laws online.
Each project was developed in partnership with a different media outlet, which ensured the reach of diverse audiences and significantly expanded the population's knowledge of the Chamber's actions, enhancing the impact of listening and citizen participation activities.
In short, the projects transform the Chamber from a distant institution into an active and itinerant presence, using communication to strengthen cooperation and expand the empowerment of the population.

name: Ouvidoria Ativa: Dados que Viram Ação Antirracista
org: Ouvidoria do Ministério da Igualdade Racial
desc: Ouvidoria Ativa: Dados que Viram Ação Antirracista is a pioneering initiative by Brazil's Ministry of Racial Equality that partnered with ride-hailing and delivery platforms—Uber, 99, iFood, Lalamove, and InDrive—to embed anti-racist educational messages directly into their apps. Building on racism complaints received—including cases targeting Afro-Brazilian religious practitioners—the Ombudsman designed segmented messages for each user profile (customers, drivers, delivery workers). Since January 2025, over a hundred awareness messages have reached millions of Brazilians through platforms they use daily, establishing a new model for integrating ombudsman functions with institutional anti-racism communication at scale.
details:
"The Racial Equality Ombudsman of the Ministry of Racial Equality (MIR) has the mission of acting as a direct bridge between the State and the population, especially historically marginalized groups. Its role goes beyond receiving complaints or reports, functioning as a strategic space for listening, articulation, and political advocacy. Within these responsibilities, the initiative we highlight here is the unprecedented integration between the functions of ombudsman and institutional communication which, through an institutional partnership, has promoted the fight against racism and the promotion of racial equality on digital platforms through the dissemination of anti-racist educational messages.

Based on receiving complaints of racism (many with religious motivation, such as against people of African-based religions in traditional clothing), perpetrated by app drivers against passengers or by customers against delivery drivers, the MIR Ombudsman established a Technical Cooperation Agreement with AMOBITEC - the Brazilian Association of Mobility and Technology (which includes companies such as Uber, 99, iFood, and Lalamove) and with the company InDrive. Through this agreement..." Based on communication guidelines from the MIR's Special Communication Advisory Office, these platforms began disseminating segmented anti-racist educational messages to drivers, delivery workers, and customers.

Since January 2025, the initiative has been active and has already published over a hundred pieces of content targeted at the audiences registered on the platforms. This is an innovative experience that combines the use of data from ombudsman offices with initiatives from the Ministry of Racial Equality to support mass communication actions, promoting behavioral change and collective awareness.

The initiative articulates listening, strategic analysis, and institutional mobilization, representing a new approach for public ombudsman offices as actors of inclusive communication with transformative potential.

name: Programa de Inovação do Tesouro do Estado
org: Subsecretraia Tesouro do Estado do Rio Grane do Sul
desc: The Treasury Innovation Program (PIT), launched in 2019 by Rio Grande do Sul’s Finance Secretariat, promotes a more efficient, transparent, and data-driven public administration through collaboration with citizens, academia, and technology partners. The program has introduced innovative tools such as the RS Servidor App for 340,000 public employees, the Climate Crisis Transparency Panel to track disaster-related public spending, and the Debt Portal to provide accessible and up-to-date information on state debt and finances. It also strengthens public understanding and participation through initiatives like the "Simpler LDO" booklet, which uses plain language to explain the state budget planning process.
details:
"The Treasury Innovation Program (PIT) was established in 2019 by the Finance Secretariat of Rio Grande do Sul to make public administration more efficient, transparent, and data-driven. It promotes innovation through co-creation and collaboration with various social, academic, and technological actors. The program is organized into seven strategic axes, including the relationship with citizens to promote greater participation, transparency in public processes, and improved spending to enhance services. There are different tools, platforms, practices, and devices that facilitate access to information. Three examples are highlighted here that are anchored in public communication practices to promote transparency, accountability, broad access to public services, participation in decisions, and dialogue between the State, government, and society.

APP Servidor: The Treasury had a high number of requests from employees for clarifications, services, and guidance on their professional lives. The demands were met by email, telephone, and in-person service. The first step was to carefully listen to the employees and pensioners, detect dissatisfactions, and gather information and suggestions to improve the quality of dialogue and speed in..." Services and prompt information exchange between the State and its employees. This dialogue was the genesis of the RS Server App, which serves 340,000 employees online, via cell phone.
The RS Climate Crisis Transparency Panel consists of data visualization for the management of budgetary resources. In May 2024, RS was hit by the country's biggest climate catastrophe. Excessive rainfall caused floods and destruction that directly affected 478 of the 497 municipalities in Rio Grande do Sul. Faced with the collapse of technological systems, the creation of the Panel became an institutional response of digital resilience, to offer society, the press and government agencies a transparent, accessible and reliable tool for analyzing the impacts of the climate crisis in the State.

The Debt Portal informs the public debate on debt with data updated monthly. It provides the values ​​of liabilities, the evolution of the outstanding balance, information on debt service – which is the amount actually paid by the State to honor debts – with data from the last 12 months and projections for the coming years. The platform presents a timeline with the main historical milestones.

The "Simpler LDO" booklet explains the budget cycle and summarizes the content of chapters and annexes of the Budget Guidelines Law Project. In 2025, its content was improved and new technical revisions were made, using Simple Language to explain the terms used in the public budget planning cycle.

name: A linguagem reduzindo a regressão penal
org: Tribunal de Justiça do Estado do Ceará
desc: A Linguagem Reduzindo a Regressão Penal (Language Reducing Penal Regression) is a plain language communication initiative by the Ceará Court of Justice Innovation Lab in the Criminal Enforcement Court of Icó. Identifying a recurring problem—inmates in semi-open regimes returning to closed prisons not due to re-offending but to inadvertent non-compliance with incomprehensible conditions—the team redesigned all prisoner communications using plain language: short sentences, direct vocabulary, practical examples, and visual support. A physical reference card was also distributed at hearings. Implementation data showed the complete elimination of involuntary regime regressions—a low-cost, high-impact intervention demonstrating how linguistic accessibility in judicial communication directly protects fundamental rights.
details:
"The initiative was developed within the Innovation Laboratory of the Court of Justice of the State of Ceará (Tribunal de Justiça do Estado do Ceará), in the Criminal Execution Court of the Icó District, with the objective of reducing regressions of regime motivated by involuntary non-compliance with the conditions imposed on people in semi-open regime. The identified problem was recurrent: many convicts returned to a different regime not due to criminal recidivism, but because they did not fully understand complex rules, transmitted in technical and inaccessible language during hearings.

The initiative consisted of a complete reorganization of public communication directed at this audience. The guidelines began to be transmitted in simple language, with short sentences, direct vocabulary, practical examples, and visual support. In addition to the oral explanation, a physical reference material was created, delivered exclusively at the admonitory hearing, allowing convicts to revisit the information whenever necessary. The focus was not on increasing control or supervision, but on ensuring a real understanding of the obligations and consequences.

The direct target audience is people serving sentences in the semi-open regime." The semi-open prison system, a group historically marked by low legal literacy and frequent exclusion from state communication processes, was developed and implemented as a controlled experiment, comparing historical data from the judicial unit. The results indicated the elimination of regressions due to negligence, maintaining only those resulting from new crimes, in addition to consistent reports of greater understanding, reduced doubts, and active use of the delivered material. The overall reduction in re-incarceration was approximately 31.54%.

The innovative nature of the initiative lies in treating language as an instrument of public policy and a variable with measurable impact, not merely as an aesthetic resource. By applying principles of plain language, information design, and behavioral science in a sensitive context such as the prison system, the project demonstrates that clear communication can produce concrete effects: harm reduction, greater institutional efficiency, and inclusion of groups traditionally left on the margins of public debate.

name: Busca ativa no Sistema Nacional de Adoção e Acolhimento: uma campanha de comunicação com histórias de famílias reunidas pela tecnologia do Programa Justiça 4.0
org: Programa das Nações Unidas para o Desenvolvimento (PNUD) e Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ)
desc: The Justice 4.0 Program used compelling storytelling to highlight the National Adoption and Foster Care System’s (SNA) active search functionality, which helps connect children and adolescents—especially those facing greater barriers to adoption—with qualified families. Through real-life family stories shared in reports, mini-documentaries, and an interactive e-book, the campaign demonstrated how technology and communication can humanize adoption and strengthen every child's right to a safe and loving family environment. Developed through cooperation between Brazil’s National Council of Justice (CNJ) and UNDP, the initiative increased public awareness of adoption while providing a replicable model for engaging citizens with complex public policies.
details:
"The integrated campaign of the Justice 4.0 Program translated the complexity of adoption into understandable and moving stories, highlighting the active search functionality of the National Adoption and Foster Care System (SNA). Using multi-format storytelling, the initiative showed how technology and communication can connect institutionalized children and adolescents with qualified families, strengthening the fundamental right of every child to grow up in a welcoming, safe, and affectionate environment.

Launched in 2019 by the National Council of Justice (CNJ), the SNA unified national registries on a digital platform that centralizes data from all Brazilian courts on children and adolescents in foster care and people eligible to adopt.

Since 2024, the system has been improved by the Justice 4.0 Program. A result of cooperation between the CNJ and the UNDP, the initiative is dedicated to developing technological solutions that make the Brazilian justice system more efficient, accessible, and closer to society.

The active search is one of the most innovative functionalities of the SNA. It connects qualified prospective adoptive parents." The tool focuses on profiles of children and adolescents who face greater barriers to adoption, such as sibling groups, children who are past early childhood, or those living with disabilities. Through photos, videos, and information, the tool humanizes the process and expands the possibilities of finding families.

To give visibility to this functionality, Justiça 4.0 developed, between 2024 and 2025, an integrated communication campaign that offered Brazilian society an experience of affective immersion. To this end, the Communication team mapped, in the courts of the North, Central-West, and South regions of Brazil, real stories of families formed thanks to the SNA's active search resource.

As a result, five original narratives were published in the form of reports and mini-documentaries on the CNJ and UNDP websites and social media. The productions also gained translated versions in English and Spanish, taking the initiative to an international audience.

Stories like that of Nathalia and Peter, who welcomed four siblings from Rio de Janeiro; that of Tamiris and Natane, who found Natan after two years of waiting; The stories of Vanessa and Gustavo, who embraced late adoption, illustrate the concrete impact of the system's functionality. Each account reinforces that the SNA (National Adoption System) is more than just technology: it's a sensitive bridge between worlds, capable of transforming lives.

Subsequently, these stories were compiled into an interactive e-book, launched in May 2025 during Adoption Month in Brazil. The campaign thus completed an eight-month cycle of activation around the technological solution.

The campaign also demonstrated potential for replicability in other contexts and initiatives that seek to bring citizens closer to complex public policies, by promoting inclusive dialogue and active listening, and giving voice to the families and children involved.

name: Transparência que Conecta: Inovação, Acesso e Participação
org: Secretaria Municipal de Integridade e Transparência da Prefeitura do Rio de Janeiro
desc: Transparência que Conecta (Transparency that Connects) is a Rio de Janeiro City Hall initiative integrating public transparency, institutional communication, civic education, and innovation. It continuously improves the Transparency Portal using plain language and user-centered design guided by Google Analytics data, while promoting civic education through educational games ('Fato ou Fake: Transparência'), interactive workshops, and territorial outreach. In 2025, the portal registered 825,000+ accesses and received 2,382 information requests with 96% answered within legal deadlines. Nationally recognized for technical quality, the initiative demonstrates how institutional transparency can be transformed from a compliance exercise into a meaningful civic engagement strategy.
details:
"Transparency that Connects: Innovation, Access, and Participation" is an initiative that integrates public transparency, institutional communication, civic education, and innovation to bring the population closer to government data and processes. It is based on the principle that transparency only generates impact when it is understandable, accessible, and capable of promoting dialogue, combining digital and territorial actions that make public management clearer and closer to the people.
The program brings together continuous improvements to the Transparency Portal, guided by simple language and reorganization of content to facilitate navigation, always respecting the complexity of public information. Decisions are guided by Google Analytics, which identifies navigation patterns and most searched content, allowing for constant adjustments based on evidence.
The initiative also promotes civic education through innovative strategies. Educational games were developed: "Fact or Fake: Transparency," "In Search of the Perfect Diamond," and "Operation Transparency: The Mystery 404," which address integrity, the right of access to information, and governance in a playful way. Soon, the children's book Clara and the Guardians of Transparency will be launched, and The podcast "Café com TransparêncIA" (Coffee with Transparency), which deals with public transparency issues and uses artificial intelligence to generate mind maps that facilitate the understanding of the content, strengthening the culture of transparency among different audiences and age groups.
In the territory, the program materializes through the Itinerant Transparency program, which will bring services, guidance, and educational activities to schools, public facilities, communities, and events. The exhibition "Transparency in Everyday Life: Informed Society" brought citizens closer to the municipal administration with visual explanations and simple language. Workshops and discussion groups also expand these spaces for listening and dialogue. The initiative also strengthens public debate by participating in events such as Rio Innovation Week, in the "Transparency in Context 5.0" panel, and the Carioca Congress of Public Integrity, in the "Transparency and Citizenship in Times of Transformation" panel.
With the direct involvement of the Transparency Coordination Office of the Rio de Janeiro City Hall, the initiative mobilizes secretariats as partners in disseminating a culture of transparency, encouraging good internal practices and strengthening processes that contribute to the sustainability of the municipal policy on access to information. The audience reached includes citizens in general, students, civil servants, researchers, communicators, and groups historically less represented by digital public communication.

The innovation in "Transparency that Connects" lies in the combination of evidence, simple language, educational resources, emerging technologies, and territorial presence. By uniting information, dialogue, and participation, it transforms transparency into a living process, contributing to a more open democracy that is closer to the people."

name: Dignidade 60+: Comunicação e Proteção Integral à Pessoa Idosa
org: Tribunal de Justiça do Estado do Ceará (TJCE)
desc: Dignidade 60+ is a public communication and social justice ecosystem by the Ceará State Court of Justice securing rights and recognition for elderly people in Ceará, Brazil. The initiative brings essential services—free legal consultations and DNA tests via the Cejusc 60+—to shopping centers and university campuses, breaking the judiciary's institutional walls. It combines direct service delivery with academic production through an International Seminar on Elder Abuse and awareness workshops. In 2025, the initiative received first place in the Gandhi Communication Award for its video celebrating active aging—establishing a model for how courts can use public communication as a vehicle for social justice and elderly rights promotion.
details:
"The Dignity 60+ initiative is a public communication and social justice ecosystem that aims to ensure the protagonism, protection, and access to rights of the elderly population in Ceará. The project unifies a series of strategic actions developed by the Commission for the Defense of the Elderly of the TJCE (Court of Justice of Ceará) in partnership with the University of Fortaleza (UNIFOR) and the State Government.

The initiative breaks down the walls of the Judiciary by bringing essential services to high-traffic spaces, such as shopping malls and university campuses, providing legal assistance, free DNA testing via Cejusc 60+ (Special Civil Court for the Elderly) and cultural activities that celebrate aging as a privilege. In addition to direct assistance, the project promotes academic production and global debate through the International Seminar on Combating Violence against the Elderly, which mobilizes national and international voices to confront physical, psychological, and patrimonial abuse. Another fundamental pillar is the 60+ Empowerment Workshops, which offer training and active listening, transforming the elderly from spectators into subjects of rights.

The project is innovative." By integrating public communication into swift judicial practice, as demonstrated by the General Inspectorate's recommendation for concentrated efforts to expedite cases involving the elderly and by the hearing task forces that prioritize dignity and listening. By combining awareness campaigns on social media, high-level scientific events, and mobile justice services, the "60+ Living with Dignity" program creates a multi-sectoral protection network that combats isolation and ageism, establishing a new standard of institutional care for the elderly.

name: Diplomacy Berlin and PlusFortyNine
desc: Diplomacy Berlin and PlusFortyNine are two interconnected editorial platforms by Novalis Medienhaus in Berlin combining journalism, storytelling, and collaboration with embassies and EU institutions to make international affairs accessible to broad audiences. Diplomacy Berlin fills a gap in diplomatic communication through long-form interviews, newsletters, press briefings, and the Diplo-Talk podcast. PlusFortyNine focuses on migration and cultural understanding for multilingual communities. Together, they have featured ambassadors, senior EU officials, and multilateral representatives, and are recognized as trusted communication bridges within Berlin's diplomatic ecosystem—demonstrating how specialized media can serve as public communication infrastructure for complex institutional audiences.
details:
"Diplomacy Berlin and PlusFortyNine are two interconnected editorial platforms developed by Novalis Medienhaus in Berlin to improve public communication around diplomacy, migration, and cultural understanding. Together, they form a new model for how media can strengthen transparency, dialogue, and trust between institutions and the public.

Diplomacy Berlin was launched to fill a growing gap in how international affairs are communicated to broad audiences. Although Berlin is one of Europe’s most active diplomatic hubs, much of its diplomatic life remains inaccessible to the public. The platform responds to this by combining journalism, storytelling, and direct collaboration with embassies, EU institutions, and international organizations. Through long-form interviews, newsletters, press briefings, and the Diplo-Talk podcast, Diplomacy Berlin humanizes global affairs and explains policy shifts, negotiations, and cultural diplomacy in formats that are accessible, rigorous, and multilingual.

PlusFortyNine complements this work by focusing on cultural integration and the lived experiences of migrants and newcomers in Germany. Built by a team that has made Germany their chosen home, it offers resources, insights, and narratives that help people understand the country’s social norms, political values, and everyday culture. Its aim is simple: reduce the friction that often accompanies migration by providing clear, empathetic communication that helps people feel oriented, informed, and included.

The two platforms were developed between 2023 and 2025 and operate with a growing network of diplomats, civil society organizations, local authorities, researchers, journalists, and Berlin-based cultural actors. Their audiences range from diplomats, policymakers, and international professionals to migrants, students, and globally curious readers looking for credible analysis and practical guidance.

The innovation lies in how the initiative bridges two often-separated domains: high-level diplomacy and everyday integration. Instead of treating them as isolated conversations, Diplomacy Berlin and PlusFortyNine bring them into the same ecosystem. International relations become more relatable when paired with human stories of identity, belonging, and cultural understanding. Migration becomes easier to navigate when contextualized within Germany’s diplomatic landscape, global debates, and policy frameworks.

The platforms also experiment with new formats for public communication combining podcasts, newsletters, community engagement, hybrid press events, and co-created content with diplomatic missions. This approach challenges traditional, top-down communication from state actors by creating a participatory space where institutions and the public engage through storytelling, dialogue, and shared learning.
"

name: DIGITAL JUSTICE AND HUMAN RIGHTS IN ANGOLA
desc: Digital Justice and Human Rights in Angola strengthens Angola's Ombudsperson's Office—the constitutional body mandated to protect citizens' rights—through digital infrastructure supported by UNDP. Since 2017, UNDP improved policies, staff competencies, and public awareness of available justice services. In 2022, IT equipment established 44 virtual hearing sites across all 18 provinces, enabling citizens to report rights violations remotely. The first virtual hearing room was inaugurated in June 2025 in Luanda. Citizen complaints grew from 4,424 in 2022 to 7,386 in 2023, reflecting increased access and public trust. The initiative models how digital infrastructure can expand ombudsman services in countries where geography limits access to institutional justice mechanisms.
details:
"The “Digital Justice and Human Rights in Angola” initiative strengthens the Ombudsperson’s Office an independent institution mandated by the 2010 Constitution to promote and protect citizens’ rights and ensure the legality of public administration. Since 2017, UNDP has supported the institution by improving policies, procedures, regulations, staff competencies, and public awareness of available justice and human rights services.
In 2022, UNDP procured IT equipment to establish 44 municipal virtual sites across all 18 provinces. This investment created conditions for citizens nationwide to access Virtual Hearing Rooms, allowing them to report human rights violations and civic injustices without needing to travel long distances. These digital platforms expand access to justice, strengthen oversight of public services, and empower citizens particularly vulnerable groups to make their voices heard.
The current phase focuses on mobilizing additional resources to expand and operationalize the Virtual Hearing Rooms, enhance technical capacity, and scale community outreach and behavioral change interventions. While the project is currently operational in Luanda (Viana and Talatona), equipment is already installed for expansion in other provinces.
The initiative is innovative because it integrates digital transformation with human rights protection, reducing structural and geographic barriers to justice. By enabling remote interaction with the Ombudsperson’s Office, it promotes institutional transparency, accountability, and more inclusive public service delivery.
Stakeholders include the Ombudsperson’s Office, the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, local authorities, civil society organizations, and community-level Human Rights Committees. UNDP provides technical leadership and coordination, drawing on its global experience and strong partnerships to strengthen governance and expand the reach of justice services in Angola.
"

name: Bora Entender
desc: Bora Entender (Let's Understand) is a weekly live programme on TV Câmara—Brazil's parliamentary television channel—that simplifies complex legislative topics in plain language. Anchored by a journalist with legislative consultants as guests, the programme accepts live audience questions via social media and phone. Broadcast nationally via Broadcast system (1,600+ municipalities), YouTube, and social networks, an episode on Tax Reform alone received 12,000+ YouTube views. Bora Entender exemplifies how legislative institutions can use public broadcasting to close the gap between lawmaking and citizen understanding—making parliamentary work genuinely accessible.
details:
"The Bora Entender program was created from the interest of TV Câmara and the Legislative Consultancy of the Chamber of Deputies in facilitating the understanding of the projects and legislative processes that are discussed and voted on in Parliament. The idea of the program is to simplify and detail, with simple language, topics often difficult to understand with the aim of reducing the distance between the citizen and the laws that guide their citizenship.

Bora Entender is an interview program anchored by a journalist and presented live from the TV Câmara studio, with the participation of legislative consultants. The topics are always chosen among those with the greatest repercussion in society and the public can ask questions that are answered during the program. The Chamber's consultants are specialists in various areas of knowledge who technically advise the deputies in the formulation of laws. And, in some cases, technical specialists linked to the Executive Branch also participate in the debate."

name: Socio-educational Reporters
org: Making Justice Programme (Programa Fazendo Justiça) – United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and National Council of Justice (CNJ Brazil)
desc: Socio-educational Reporters is a journalism workshop created by UNDP's Making Justice Programme (in partnership with Brazil's National Council of Justice) for adolescents serving socio-educational measures in Brazil's juvenile justice system. The initiative trained young people to cover the 2025 Literary Pathways event—an annual cultural program for youth in socio-educational facilities—shifting their role from news subjects to authors. In the 4th edition, 84 facilities across all 27 Brazilian states participated. The adolescents' journalism ensured decentralized, regionally diverse coverage, and the approach received strong CNJ backing as a model for youth-centered communication in justice contexts.
details:
"Through the Making Justice Programme, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) partners with the National Council of Justice (CNJ) to deliver transformative actions within Brazil’s criminal and socio-educational (juvenile justice) systems. 
Since 2022, the Programme organises annually the  Literary Pathways in the Socio-educational System (Caminhos Literários no Socioeducativo), an event that brings together hundreds of adolescents serving socio-educational measures in virtual and in-person activities focused on culture and artistic expression, including lectures, workshops, and musical and audiovisual performances prepared by the young participants themselves. In its 4th edition (2025), the event engaged 84 participating facilities, with representatives from all 27 federative units of Brazil. 
The project was developed by the Making Justice Programme’s Communication team  and involved creating a journalism workshop for adolescents, aimed at training them to carry out journalistic coverage of the event. 
Sixteen adolescents (including two girls and one transgender boy) from five socio‑educational facilities took part in the workshops. These facilities were selected from nearly 40 applications to represent Brazil’s five macro‑regions. Selection also considered existing communication infrastructure and previous projects in the field. 
The project reaffirms communication as a human right, ensures protagonism for a historically marginalized group, and amplifies the voices of these adolescents. The youths’ final productions, including video reports, written articles, and photographs, were disseminated internally within each facility. A short video was also shared on UNDP Brazil’s social media channels, with due attention to privacy and the protection of participants’ identities. 
A survey conducted with socio-educational staff responsible for the participating adolescents indicated a positive impact of the initiative on both individual trajectories and daily life within the facilities. The professionals reported there was high engagement throughout the training and journalistic coverage, as well as strong comprehension and practical application of the content. Improvements were observed in skills such as active listening, organising ideas, teamwork, and oral and written communication, alongside strengthened self-esteem and a greater sense of belonging, as their narratives were recognized and disseminated. 
The project is also noteworthy for its intersectoral nature, with impacts across the fields of Justice, Culture, Education, and Communication. 
The initiative is expected to be expanded to additional facilities during the coverage of the 2026 edition of Literary Pathways. The project can be easily replicated in facilities with minimal recording infrastructure, as editing can be done using mobile devices."

name: “TUJENGE AMANI PAMOYA” Programme de dialogue intergénérationnel pour la confiance, la collaboration et la cohésion sociale
org: Laboratoire Interdisciplinaire du Développement Social LAIDES/Université de Goma
desc: Tujenge Amani Pamoya ('Let's Build Peace Together') is an intergenerational dialogue programme by the LAIDES research laboratory at the University of Goma in eastern DRC. Responding to persistent distrust between youth and elders, the programme combines academic expertise with community anchoring to strengthen social cohesion through structured dialogue methodologies. At the November 2025 Pole Institute event, participants observed notable reductions in intergenerational tensions and emergence of joint peaceful coexistence commitments—with youth leaders, religious authorities, and elders expressing renewed trust. The programme validates dialogue-based communication as a peacebuilding tool in conflict-affected communities.
details:
“Tujenge Amani Pamoya,” meaning “Let’s Build Peace Together,” is a public communication and intergenerational dialogue program led by the Interdisciplinary Laboratory for Social Development (LAIDES), a research center affiliated with the University of Goma. It combines academic expertise with the community roots of participants and local leaders to strengthen social cohesion and intergenerational trust in eastern DRC.
The initiative addresses a major challenge: the persistent mistrust between young and old, exacerbated by gerontocracy and a lack of inclusive dialogue. It aims to:
• Reduce intergenerational mistrust and misunderstandings.
• Foster constructive and inclusive dialogue, based on active listening and respect for pluralism.
• Develop a structured public communication methodology adaptable to other contexts.
• Create sustainable spaces for exchange between young leaders, community leaders, religious leaders, and elders, generating shared commitments to peaceful coexistence.
Target audience and stakeholders: Young community and religious leaders, influencers, elders and traditional leaders, community and religious leaders, and citizens participating in the dialogues.

Innovation: The program transforms public communication into a concrete tool for reducing tensions, building trust, and fostering cooperation. It is based on an intergenerational dialogue organized by Pole Institute on November 27, 2025, in Goma, the provincial capital of North Kivu, which was then capitalized on and systematized by LAIDES to develop a replicable methodology. The emphasis is on active listening, respectful dialogue, and co-creation, offering strong potential for replication in other regions of the Global South and contributing to peaceful, inclusive, and sustainable local governance.

"

name: Terre et Femme – Communication publique inclusive pour les droits des femmes et l’environnement
desc: Terre et Femme is a social innovation and inclusive public communication initiative in Benin that makes public policies on women's rights, environment, and sustainable development more accessible and appropriable for local populations. Using citizen journalism, educational outreach, and social storytelling, the initiative translates technical public commitments into clear, culturally relevant messages for women, youth, and local communities. Stakeholders include civil society actors, media, public institutions, and community leaders. Since its creation, Terre et Femme has strengthened public access to gender and environmental rights information and increased visibility of underreported topics—building a more informed and engaged citizenry in West Africa.
details:
"Terre et Femme is a social innovation and inclusive public communication initiative in Benin that aims to make public policies related to women's rights, the environment, and sustainable development more accessible, understandable, and embraced by the population.
The initiative uses a citizen journalism, educational outreach, and social storytelling approach to translate often technical public texts, programs, and commitments into clear, contextualized, and culturally relevant messages.
Terre et Femme primarily targets women, youth, and local communities, while also involving civil society actors, the media, public institutions, and community leaders as stakeholders.
Activities include producing informational and awareness-raising content, disseminating information digitally on social media, covering public and community initiatives, and highlighting citizen testimonies.
Terre et Femme's innovative nature lies in its ability to integrate public communication, human rights, and citizen participation within a local context, prioritizing accessible and inclusive formats. The initiative thus contributes to strengthening understanding of public policies." "Transparency in public action and civic engagement, particularly in developing countries."

name: Denuncia.org
desc: Denuncia.org is a digital platform by Impunidad Cero launched in 2020 to help crime victims in Mexico understand how to file complaints. In a country where over 93% of crimes go unreported largely due to bureaucratic complexity, the platform uses technology to translate dense legal language into accessible guidance—offering a court agency locator, specialized reporting guides, and simplified procedural information. Since launch, it has registered 1,834,802 unique users and 2,194,378 sessions, and received the 2022 Latin American Digital Democracy Award. Originally focused on ordinary citizens, it became a key resource for legal professionals and civil society organizations—demonstrating how civic technology can reduce barriers to justice.
details:
Denuncia.org is an initiative of Impunidad Cero (Zero Impunity), launched in September 2020 with the support of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation. Its purpose is to offer simple and accessible information so that any victim of a crime in Mexico can understand what they need, where to go, and how to file a complaint. The platform is designed to combat the dark figure of crime in Mexico, where more than 93% of crimes are neither reported nor investigated, largely due to bureaucratic complexity and a lack of understanding of the criminal process. Although the focus is on the average citizen, the tool has become a vital resource for justice system operators, law students, and civil society organizations in Mexico.

Denuncia.org's innovation lies in its use of technology to translate the technical and legal language of criminal procedure into accessible language. The platform offers a set of practical tools, including a locator for Public Prosecutor's offices, a directory of digital complaint platforms available to state prosecutors for filing online complaints, downloadable forms, and a directory of more than 400 legal support organizations. Psychological. By bringing everything necessary together in one place, it makes it easier for victims of crime to reach the nearest agency to file a report, prepared, informed, and with realistic expectations about their process."
